title.en: Volume 303 Biographies 62: Zhang Wenzhi, Wei Guan, Teng Zongliang, Li Fang, Zhao Xiang, Tang Su, Zhang Shu, Huang Zhen, Hu Shunzhi, Chen Guan, Fan Xiang, Tian Jing
title.raw: 卷三百〇三 列傳第六十二 張昷之 魏瓘 滕宗諒 李防 趙湘 唐肅 張述 黃震 胡順之 陳貫 范祥 田京 Volume 303 Biographies 62: Zhang Wenzhi, Wei Guan, Teng Zongliang, Li Fang, Zhao Xiang, Tang Su, Zhang Shu, Huang Zhen, Hu Shunzhi, Chen Guan, Fan Xiang, Tian Jing

sentences.zh: 張昷之

translations.literal: Zhang Wenzhi
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenzhi

sentences.zh: 張昷之，字景山。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenzhi, courtesy name Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenzhi, whose courtesy name was Jingshan,

sentences.zh: 父秘，自有傳。

translations.literal: His father Mi has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Mi is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 昷之進士及第，補樂清尉，潤州觀察推官，校勘館閣書籍，遷集賢校理，通判常州，知溫州。

translations.literal: Wenzhi passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Yueqing assistant magistrate, Runzhou surveillance commissioner staff officer, collator of palace library books, promoted to Jixian collator, served as vice-prefect of Changzhou, and was prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, Wenzhi served successively as assistant magistrate of Yueqing, staff officer to the Runzhou surveillance commissioner, and collator of palace library books; he was then promoted to collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, made vice-prefect of Changzhou, and appointed prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 蔡齊薦其材可用，擢提點淮南路刑獄。

translations.literal: Cai Qi recommended that his talent could be used, and he was promoted to judicial intendant of the Huainan East circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Qi recommended him as a man of proven ability, and he was promoted to judicial intendant for the Huainan East circuit.

sentences.zh: 楊崇勳知亳州，恃恩為不法，誣蒙城知縣王申罪，械送獄。

translations.literal: Yang Chongxun was prefect of Bozhou; relying on favor he acted unlawfully, falsely charged Mengcheng magistrate Wang Shen with a crime, and sent him to prison in fetters.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chongxun, prefect of Bozhou, abused imperial favor to break the law: he framed Mengcheng magistrate Wang Shen on false charges and had him sent to prison in chains.

sentences.zh: 昷之廉得冤狀，乃出申，配奸吏若干人。

translations.literal: Wenzhi through investigation obtained the facts of the injustice, then released Shen and banished several corrupt clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhi investigated the case, found that Shen had been wronged, released him, and banished several corrupt subordinates.

sentences.zh: 徙廣南東路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be transport commissioner of the Guangnan East circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to serve as transport commissioner for the Guangnan East circuit.

sentences.zh: 夷人有犯，其酋長得自治而多慘酷，請一以漢法從事。

translations.literal: When Yi people committed offenses, their chieftains were allowed to judge them autonomously and were often cruel; he requested that Han law alone be applied.
translations.idiomatic: When tribal offenders were involved, local chieftains were allowed to try them under their own customs, often with excessive cruelty; he petitioned that all such cases be handled solely under Han law.

sentences.zh: 權度支判官，為京西轉運使，加直史館，徙河北。

translations.literal: He served as acting revenue-section judge, became Jingxi transport commissioner, was added to the Direct Historiography, and was transferred to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting judge in the Revenue Section, was appointed transport commissioner for the Jingxi circuit, was given appointment to the Direct Historiography, and was transferred to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 被邊諸州發卒斬西山木，卒逃入契丹者歲數百人，敵既利其所開地，又得亡卒，故不急。

translations.literal: Border prefectures sent soldiers to cut timber on the western hills; each year several hundred soldiers fled into Khitan territory. The enemy profited from the land they opened and also gained the deserters, so they were not urgent about it.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier prefectures sent troops to fell timber in the western hills, and every year several hundred soldiers deserted into Khitan territory. The Khitan benefited from the cleared land and welcomed the runaways, so they made no effort to stop the practice.

sentences.zh: 昷之戒斬伐毋得深入北地，卒亦不敢逃。

translations.literal: Wenzhi warned that logging must not penetrate deep into the northern lands, and the soldiers also did not dare flee.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhi ordered that logging parties must not penetrate deep into the northern frontier, and thereafter the soldiers no longer dared to desert.

sentences.zh: 還，為鹽鐵副使，擢天章閣待制、河北都轉運按察使。

translations.literal: On his return he became vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Commission, was promoted to Hanlin associate at the Tianzhang Pavilion, and was made Hebei chief transport and inspection commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to court he was made vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Commission, then promoted to Hanlin associate at the Tianzhang Pavilion and appointed chief transport and inspection commissioner for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 保州、廣信、安肅軍自五代以來別領兵萬人，號緣邊都巡檢司，亦曰策先鋒，以知州、軍為使，置副二人，分所領卒為三部，使援鄰道。

translations.literal: Baozhou, Guangxin, and Ansu garrisons since the Five Dynasties separately commanded ten thousand troops, called the Frontier General Inspection Office, also called the Vanguard Strategy [unit]; the prefect or garrison commander served as commissioner, with two deputies appointed, dividing the troops under command into three sections to reinforce neighboring circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Five Dynasties, Baozhou, Guangxin, and Ansu had each maintained a separate force of ten thousand men under the Frontier General Inspection Office, also known as the Vanguard Strategy command. The prefect or garrison commander served as commissioner, with two deputies; the force was divided into three divisions to reinforce neighboring circuits.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗用之有功，詔每出巡別給糧錢以優之。

translations.literal: Taizu once used them with merit; an edict ordered that on each patrol they be separately given grain money as a favor.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had once employed them with success, and an edict provided extra grain and cash whenever they went on patrol as a special reward.

sentences.zh: 其後州將不復出，內侍為副，數出巡，部卒偏得廩賜，軍中以為不均。

translations.literal: Afterward the prefectural generals no longer went out; eunuchs served as deputies and frequently went on patrol, and the troops under them alone received stipends and rewards; the army regarded this as unfair.
translations.idiomatic: Later the prefectural commanders ceased to lead patrols themselves; eunuch deputies went out frequently instead, and only the troops under the patrolling division received extra rations and bonuses, which the rest of the army regarded as unjust.

sentences.zh: 通判保州石待舉言於昷之，請合三部兵更出入，季一出即別給錢糧，餘悉罷，仍請以武臣代內侍。

translations.literal: Baozhou vice-prefect Shi Daiju spoke to Wenzhi, requesting that the three divisions' troops rotate in going out, that when one division went out each season it alone receive separate money and grain, that the rest all be abolished, and still requesting that military officials replace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhou vice-prefect Shi Daiju proposed to Wenzhi that the three divisions rotate patrol duty, with only the division on active patrol each season receiving the extra pay and rations, that all other special allowances be abolished, and that military officers replace the eunuch deputies.

sentences.zh: 時楊懷敏方任邊事，尤不悅巡檢司。

translations.literal: At the time Yang Huaimin was just then in charge of frontier affairs and especially disliked the inspection office.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huaimin was then in charge of frontier affairs and particularly resented the inspection office.

sentences.zh: 雲翼卒惡石待舉，遂殺之以作亂。

translations.literal: Yunyijun soldiers hated Shi Daiju and therefore killed him to raise a rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Yunyijun garrison troops hated Shi Daiju and murdered him in the course of a mutiny.

sentences.zh: 昷之自魏馳至城下，召諸將部分攻城，使人請懷敏曰：「不即來，當以軍法從事。」

translations.literal: Wenzhi galloped from Wei to below the city wall, summoned the generals to assign sections for assaulting the city, and sent someone to request Huaimin, saying: "If you do not come immediately, military law will be applied."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhi galloped from Wei to the besieged city, summoned the generals to organize the assault, and sent a messenger to Yang Huaimin: "Come at once, or you will answer to military law."

sentences.zh: 既至，又以兵自衛，昷之曰：「諸將方集，獨敢以兵隨，將欲反邪！」

translations.literal: When he arrived, he again came with troops to guard himself. Wenzhi said: "The generals have just assembled; you alone dare bring troops with you—do you intend to rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: When Huaimin arrived, he came surrounded by his own troops. Wenzhi said, "The generals are assembled here—do you dare bring an armed escort? Are you planning a counter-rebellion?"

sentences.zh: 叱去衛者。

translations.literal: He shouted at them to dismiss the guards.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the escort dismissed.

sentences.zh: 城開，田況潛殺降兵數百人，昷之預知其謀。

translations.literal: When the city opened, Tian Kuang secretly killed several hundred surrendered soldiers; Wenzhi had foreknown his plot.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell, Tian Kuang secretly executed several hundred surrendered troops—a move Wenzhi had anticipated.

sentences.zh: 除戶部副使，既而坐前事奪職，知虢州。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice minister of the Household Department; soon afterward because of the earlier affair his office was stripped and he was made prefect of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of the Household Department, but soon lost the post over the earlier affair and was made prefect of Guozhou instead.

sentences.zh: 王則反貝州，有言昷之在河北捕得妖人李教不殺，使得逸去，今乃為則主謀，事平，無其人。

translations.literal: Wang Ze rebelled at Beizhou; some said that when Wenzhi was in Hebei he captured the sorcerer Li Jiao but did not kill him, allowing him to escape, and that he now plotted for Ze; when the affair was settled, there was no such person.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ze rebelled at Beizhou, some accused Wenzhi of having captured the sorcerer Li Jiao in Hebei but spared him, allowing Li to escape and now mastermind Ze's revolt; after the rebellion was suppressed, no such person could be found.

sentences.zh: 會冀州人段得政詣闕，自言嘗為叔父屯田郎中曇賕免緣坐，且言曇以書屬昷之，乃下御史按劾，雖不得書，猶奪三官，監鄂州稅。

translations.literal: It happened that Jizhou man Duan Dezheng came to court, saying he had once been implicated because his uncle Director of Agriculture Duan Tan had been pardoned from punishment by connection, and also saying Tan had entrusted a letter to Wenzhi; the censorate was ordered to investigate; although the letter was not obtained, he still lost three ranks and supervised Ezhou tax collection.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile a man from Jizhou named Duan Dezheng petitioned the throne, claiming he had once been implicated when his uncle Duan Tan, a director in the Agriculture Bureau, was pardoned through favoritism, and alleging that Tan had entrusted a letter to Wenzhi. The censorate was ordered to investigate; though no letter was found, Wenzhi was still stripped of three ranks and assigned to supervise tax collection at Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 知漢陽軍，稍遷刑部郎中，復待制、知湖州，徙揚州。

translations.literal: He was military prefect of Hanyang, was gradually promoted to director in the Ministry of Punishments, again made Hanlin associate and prefect of Huzhou, and was transferred to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military prefect of Hanyang, was gradually promoted to director in the Ministry of Punishments, was restored to Hanlin associate and made prefect of Huzhou, then transferred to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以光祿卿致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He retired as Director of the Imperial Sacrifices and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the rank of Director of the Imperial Sacrifices and later died.

sentences.zh: 昷之喜吏事，所至有聲。

translations.literal: Wenzhi delighted in administrative affairs; wherever he went he had a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhi took pleasure in administrative work and won a strong reputation everywhere he served.

sentences.zh: 退居築家廟，率子弟歲時奉祠。

translations.literal: In retirement he built a family temple and led his sons and younger brothers in seasonal offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he built a family ancestral hall and led his sons and younger brothers in offering seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 魏瓘，字用之。

translations.literal: Wei Guan, courtesy name Yongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan, whose courtesy name was Yongzhi,

sentences.zh: 父羽奏補秘書省校書郎、監廣積倉，知開封府倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: His father Yu was memorialized to fill the post of Secretariat proofreader, supervised the Guangji granary, and was Kaifeng prefecture grain-section staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wei Yu entered service through memorial appointment as proofreader in the Secretariat, supervised the Guangji granary, and served as grain-section staff officer in the Kaifeng prefecture office.

sentences.zh: 持法精審，明吏事。

translations.literal: He upheld the law with precision and scrutiny and was clear in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He applied the law with meticulous care and was thoroughly versed in administrative practice.

sentences.zh: 上元起彩山，闕前張燈，與宦者護作，宦者挾氣，視瓘年少，輒誅索侵擾。

translations.literal: At the Yuan festival they raised the Brocade Mountain; lanterns were hung before the palace, and Guan worked with eunuchs to guard the construction; the eunuchs relied on their power, regarded Guan as young, and repeatedly extorted and harassed him.
translations.idiomatic: At the Lantern Festival the Brocade Mountain was erected and lanterns hung before the palace; Guan supervised the work alongside eunuch attendants, who abused their influence, took him for a young man, and repeatedly extorted and harassed him.

sentences.zh: 瓘密以聞，詔杖宦者遣之。

translations.literal: Guan secretly reported it; an edict ordered the eunuchs beaten with the staff and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Guan reported the matter in secret; the emperor ordered the eunuchs flogged and sent away.

sentences.zh: 瓘門人魏綱上疏詆天書，流海島，瓘亦坐是停官。

translations.literal: Guan's student Wei Gang submitted a memorial slandering the Heavenly Writings and was exiled to a sea island; Guan also because of this was suspended from office.
translations.idiomatic: Guan's protégé Wei Gang submitted a memorial denouncing the Heavenly Writings and was exiled to a distant island; Guan was also dismissed from office on that account.

sentences.zh: 復監鄧州稅、鄂州茶，以大理寺丞知衡山縣，通判壽州，歷知循、隨、安州，提點廣南西路刑獄。

translations.literal: He again supervised Dengzhou tax and Ezhou tea, served as Dali Temple assistant prefect of Hengshan county, vice-prefect of Shouzhou, successively prefect of Xun, Sui, and Anzhou, and judicial intendant of the Guangnan West circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reappointed to supervise tax at Dengzhou and tea at Ezhou, served as assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Hengshan, as vice-prefect of Shouzhou, and successively as prefect of Xun, Sui, and An prefectures before becoming judicial intendant for the Guangnan West circuit.

sentences.zh: 邕州獠戶緣逋負沒婦女為傭者一千餘人，悉奏還其家。

translations.literal: At Yongzhou, over a thousand Liao households' women had been seized as bond servants because of debts; he memorialized to return them all to their families.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongzhou more than a thousand women from Liao households had been seized as debt bond servants; he memorialized for their release and return to their families.

sentences.zh: 就除轉運使。

translations.literal: He was thereupon appointed transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promptly appointed transport commissioner on the spot.

sentences.zh: 劉鋹時計口以稅，雖舟居皆不免，至是而雷、化、欽、廉、高州猶未除，瓘為除之。

translations.literal: Under Liu Chang taxes were levied by head count; even those living on boats were not exempt; by this time Lei, Hua, Qin, Lian, and Gaozhou still had not abolished it, and Guan abolished it for them.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Southern Han ruler Liu Chang taxes had been levied per capita, with even boat-dwellers liable; by Guan's time Lei, Hua, Qin, Lian, and Gao prefectures still retained the practice, and he abolished it in those regions.

sentences.zh: 減柳州無名役四百人。

translations.literal: He reduced four hundred unnamed corvée laborers at Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He cut four hundred unauthorized corvée laborers at Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 召權度支判官。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as acting revenue-section judge.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as acting judge in the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 尋以罪降知洪州，徙梓州路轉運使，還知蔡州、潭州，為京西轉運使，江淮制置發運使，自主客郎中遷太常少卿，知廣州。

translations.literal: Soon because of an offense he was demoted to prefect of Hongzhou, transferred to Zizhou circuit transport commissioner, returned to be prefect of Caizhou and Tanzhou, became Jingxi transport commissioner, Huai-Jiang commissioner for transport provisioning, rose from director in the Ministry of Receptions to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was demoted for an offense to prefect of Hongzhou, then made transport commissioner for the Zizhou circuit; he later served again as prefect of Caizhou and Tanzhou, as Jingxi transport commissioner, as commissioner for Huai-Jiang transport provisioning, rose from director in the Ministry of Receptions to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was appointed prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 築州城環五里，疏東江門，鑿東西澳為水閘，以時啟閉焉。

translations.literal: He built the prefectural wall encircling five li, dredged the Dongjiang Gate, excavated the east and west harbors as sluice gates, and opened and closed them according to season.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the prefectural walls in a circuit of five li, dredged the Dongjiang Gate, and excavated the eastern and western harbors into sluice gates that were opened and closed according to the season.

sentences.zh: 拜右諫議大夫，再任臨江軍判官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee and again served as Linjiangjun staff judge.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee and served a second term as staff judge at Linjiangjun.

sentences.zh: 史沆性險詖，嘗為瓘所劾免。

translations.literal: Shi Hang by nature was treacherous and slanderous; he had once been impeached and dismissed by Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hang was treacherous and malicious by nature and had once been impeached and dismissed by Guan.

sentences.zh: 會廣州封送貢餘椰子煎等餉京師，輒邀留之，飛奏指以為珍貨，詔遣內侍發驗無有，沆坐不實廢，瓘亦降知鄂州。

translations.literal: It happened that Guangzhou sealed and sent surplus tribute of fried coconut and the like to the capital; Hang intercepted and detained them, urgently memorialized accusing them of being precious goods; an edict sent a eunuch to open and verify—there were none; Hang was punished for false accusation and dismissed; Guan was also demoted to prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzhou forwarded surplus tribute items such as fried coconut to the capital, Hang intercepted the shipment and urgently memorialized that it contained contraband valuables. The court sent a eunuch to inspect the consignment and found nothing of the kind; Hang was dismissed for a false accusation, and Guan was demoted to prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 未逾年，復為陝西轉運使，徙河北。

translations.literal: Within less than a year he again became Shaanxi transport commissioner and was transferred to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was reappointed Shaanxi transport commissioner and then transferred to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 以給事中知開封府，政事嚴明，吏民憚之。

translations.literal: As Supervising Secretary he was made Kaifeng prefect; his administration was strict and clear, and clerks and people feared him.
translations.idiomatic: As Supervising Secretary he was appointed prefect of Kaifeng; his administration was rigorous and clear, and both officials and commoners stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 內東門索命婦車，得賂遺掖庭物，付府驗治，獄未上，內降釋罪。

translations.literal: The Inner East Gate office, seeking the consort's carriage, obtained bribes of palace women's goods; he handed them to the prefecture for verification and punishment; before the case was submitted, an inner edict released them from guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When the Inner East Gate office, investigating the empress's carriage, uncovered bribes involving palace women's property, he referred the case to the prefecture for prosecution; before trial could proceed, an edict from within the palace ordered the suspects released.

sentences.zh: 諫官吳奎言法當執奏，而瓘不即奏行，請以廢法論，降知越州。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Wu Kui said the law required memorializing and enforcing, but Guan did not immediately memorialize and execute; he requested punishment for nullifying the law, and Guan was demoted to prefect of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Wu Kui argued that the law required a formal memorial before any release could take effect, and that Guan had failed to submit one before carrying out the edict; he called for punishment on grounds of nullifying the law, and Guan was demoted to prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 儂智高寇廣東、西，獨廣州城堅守不能下。

translations.literal: Nong Zhigao raided Guangdong and Guangxi; only Guangzhou's city, firmly defended, could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: When Nong Zhigao invaded Guangdong and Guangxi, Guangzhou alone held out under siege and could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 於是論築城功，遷工部侍郎、集賢院學士，復知廣州，兼廣東經略安撫使，給禁卒五千，聽以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Thereupon in consideration of the merit of building the city wall he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, again made prefect of Guangzhou, and concurrently Guangdong frontier commissioner and pacification commissioner, given five thousand palace troops, and permitted to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his merit in fortifying the city, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, reappointed prefect of Guangzhou with concurrent duties as frontier commissioner and pacification commissioner for Guangdong, granted five thousand palace troops, and authorized to act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 屬狄青已破賊，召還，糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: It happened that Di Qing had already defeated the rebels; Guan was recalled and inspected capital criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: By then Di Qing had already defeated the rebels; Guan was recalled to review capital criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 議者請開六塔河，塞商胡北流，宰相主其說，命瓘按視，還奏以為不可塞。

translations.literal: Advisers requested opening the Liuta River and blocking the Shanghu northern flow; the chief minister championed the proposal and ordered Guan to inspect on site; on his return he memorialized that it could not be blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Some officials proposed opening the Liuta River and blocking the northern channel of the Shanghu; the chief minister supported the plan and ordered Guan to inspect the site. On his return he memorialized that the northern flow could not safely be blocked.

sentences.zh: 下溪州蠻彭士羲叛，將發兵討除。

translations.literal: The Xiachixi Man chieftain Peng Shiyi rebelled; troops were about to be sent to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shiyi, a Man chieftain of Xiachixi, rebelled, and the court prepared to send troops against him.

sentences.zh: 進龍圖閣直學士、知荊南。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Dragon Diagram Pavilion academician and made prefect of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and appointed prefect of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 瓘以為「五溪之險，師行鳥道，諸將貪功生事，於國家何所利？」

translations.literal: Guan considered: "The peril of the Five Streams—troops march on bird paths; the generals, greedy for merit, stir up trouble—what profit is there for the state?"
translations.idiomatic: Guan argued, "The Five Streams country is all but impassable—troops can advance only along narrow mountain paths. Generals greedy for glory will manufacture incidents. What possible benefit could this bring the state?"

sentences.zh: 因條上三策，以招徠為上，守禦為下，功取為失。

translations.literal: He therefore itemized three policies: taking recruitment as highest, defense as lowest, and merit-seizing assault as error.
translations.idiomatic: He accordingly submitted three ranked policies: winning tribes through inducement was best, defensive containment was acceptable, and seeking glory through force was a mistake.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not reply.

sentences.zh: 後卒如瓘議。

translations.literal: Later it finally turned out as Guan had argued.
translations.idiomatic: Events later vindicated Guan's advice.

sentences.zh: 徙澶州、滑州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chunzhou and Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chunzhou and Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 又徙鄧州，不行，請老，以吏部侍郎致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Dengzhou but did not go; he requested retirement and retired as Vice Minister of Personnel, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to Dengzhou but declined to take up the post, requested retirement, retired with the rank of Vice Minister of Personnel, and died.

sentences.zh: 瓘所至整辦，與人置對未嘗屈。

translations.literal: Wherever Guan went he put things in order; in confronting others he never yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, Guan brought affairs to good order; in confrontation he never yielded.

sentences.zh: 史沆、王逵以善訟名天下，瓘既廢沆，又嘗奏抵逵罪，專任機數，不稱循吏。

translations.literal: Shi Hang and Wang Kui were famed throughout the realm for skill in litigation; Guan had already dismissed Hang and had also once memorialized to impeach Kui; he relied exclusively on stratagems and was not called a compassionate official.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hang and Wang Kui were renowned throughout the empire for their skill in litigation; Guan had already brought about Hang's dismissal and had once memorialized to impeach Kui. He relied on calculation and maneuver rather than gentle governance and was not regarded as a model compassionate official.

sentences.zh: 弟琰。

translations.literal: Younger brother Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yan.

sentences.zh: 弟 琰

translations.literal: Younger brother Yan
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Yan

sentences.zh: 琰，字子浩，以父恩授秘書省正字，為吏強敏，名齊於瓘。

translations.literal: Yan, courtesy name Zihao, received through his father's favor the Secretariat proofreader post; as an official he was forceful and keen, and his reputation equaled Guan's.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, whose courtesy name was Zihao, entered service through his father's privilege as proofreader in the Secretariat. As an official he was forceful and sharp-witted, and his reputation matched his brother's.

sentences.zh: 嘗通判陳州，適歲饑，百姓相率強取人粟，坐死者甚眾，琰曰：「此迫於窮餓，豈得已者。」

translations.literal: He once served as vice-prefect of Chenzhou; it happened to be a famine year, and the common people in groups forcibly seized others' grain; many were sentenced to death for it. Yan said: "This was forced by destitution and hunger—how could they have helped it?"
translations.idiomatic: He once served as vice-prefect of Chenzhou during a famine year when people banded together to seize grain by force; many were sentenced to death. Yan said, "They were driven to desperation by hunger—what choice did they have?"

sentences.zh: 坐其首黥之。

translations.literal: He punished only the ringleaders with tattooing.
translations.idiomatic: He punished only the ringleaders with facial tattooing.

sentences.zh: 歷知壽、潤、滁、安州。

translations.literal: He successively was prefect of Shou, Run, Chu, and Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as prefect of Shou, Run, Chu, and An prefectures.

sentences.zh: 壽州盜殺寺童子，有司執僧笞服，琰憫其非罪，命脫械縱去，一府爭以為不可，後數日得真盜。

translations.literal: At Shouzhou a thief killed a temple boy; the authorities seized a monk and beat him until he confessed; Yan pitied his innocence, ordered his fetters removed and let him go; the whole prefecture disputed that this was impermissible; several days later the real thief was caught.
translations.idiomatic: At Shouzhou a thief murdered a temple acolyte; officials seized a monk and beat him until he confessed. Yan, convinced of the monk's innocence, ordered his chains removed and set him free over the objections of the entire prefectural staff; several days later the real culprit was apprehended.

sentences.zh: 富人犯法當死而死獄中，琰曰：「是嘗欺匿異籍孤弱者財，所以自斃，覬不可窮治爾，其吏受賕而為之謀乎？」

translations.literal: A rich man violated the law, should have been executed but died in prison; Yan said: "This man once cheated and concealed the property of orphans and weak persons of different household registers; he therefore killed himself, hoping he could not be thoroughly prosecuted—did his clerks take bribes and plot for him?"
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy man who deserved execution died in prison instead. Yan said, "This man had long cheated orphans and the weak out of property registered under other households. He killed himself hoping to escape a full investigation—did his clerks take bribes and arrange this for him?"

sentences.zh: 後有告者如琰所料。

translations.literal: Later an informer appeared just as Yan had surmised.
translations.idiomatic: An informer later came forward, just as Yan had suspected.

sentences.zh: 累官司農卿、知福州，徙廣州。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he became Minister of Agriculture and was prefect of Fuzhou, then was transferred to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Minister of Agriculture, served as prefect of Fuzhou, and was transferred to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以疾告，得知江寧府。

translations.literal: He reported illness and was made prefect of Jiangning prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He reported illness and was appointed prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 晚昏毛，縱私人亂法，日笞扑無罪吏卒。

translations.literal: In his later years he was muddled and coarse, indulged private persons in disturbing the law, and daily flogged innocent clerks and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he grew muddled and harsh, allowed favorites to flout the law, and daily flogged innocent clerks and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 監司劾奏，召判刑部，乃致仕，進衛尉卿，卒。

translations.literal: Supervisory officials impeached and memorialized; he was summoned to judge cases in the Ministry of Punishments, then retired, was advanced to Director of the Imperial Guard, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory officials impeached him; he was recalled to adjudicate cases at the Ministry of Punishments, then retired, was promoted to Director of the Imperial Guard, and died.

sentences.zh: 滕宗諒

translations.literal: Teng Zongliang
translations.idiomatic: Teng Zongliang

sentences.zh: 〈劉越 附〉

translations.literal: (Liu Yue appended)
translations.idiomatic: (with appended biography of Liu Yue)

sentences.zh: 滕宗諒，字子京，河南人。

translations.literal: Teng Zongliang, courtesy name Zijing, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Zongliang, whose courtesy name was Zijing, was a native of Henan.

sentences.zh: 與范仲淹同年舉進士，其後仲淹稱其才，乃以泰州軍事推官召試學士院。

translations.literal: He and Fan Zhongyan passed the jinshi examination in the same year; afterward Zhongyan praised his talent, and he was summoned to the Hanlin examination as Taizhou military staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Fan Zhongyan; later Zhongyan praised his ability, and he was summoned from his post as staff officer at Taizhou to take the Hanlin examination.

sentences.zh: 改大理寺丞，知當塗、邵武二縣，遷殿中丞，代還。

translations.literal: He was changed to Dali Temple assistant director, was magistrate of Dangtu and Shaowu counties, was promoted to Palace Director, and returned on completion of his term.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and served as magistrate of Dangtu and Shaowu counties before being promoted to Palace Director and recalled to the capital at the end of his term.

sentences.zh: 會禁中火，詔劾火所從起，宗諒與秘書丞劉越皆上疏諫。

translations.literal: It happened that fire broke out within the forbidden precinct; an edict ordered investigation of where the fire originated; Zongliang and Secretariat assistant director Liu Yue both submitted memorials remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: When fire broke out within the palace precincts, an edict ordered an investigation into its origin; Zongliang and Secretariat assistant director Liu Yue both submitted memorials of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 宗諒曰：「伏見掖庭遺燼，延熾宮闥，雖沿人事，實繫天時。

translations.literal: Zongliang said: "I observe that embers left in the rear palace spread and blazed through the palace gates; though it follows human affairs, it is in fact tied to the seasons of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zongliang wrote, "I observe that embers left smoldering in the rear palace spread until the palace halls were ablaze. Though this began as a human accident, it truly reflects Heaven's warning.

sentences.zh: 詔書亟下，引咎滌瑕，中外莫不感動。

translations.literal: Edicts were urgently issued, taking blame and cleansing faults; within and without none were not moved.
translations.idiomatic: Your edicts followed swiftly, accepting blame and pledging reform, and court and country alike were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 然而詔獄未釋，鞫訊尚嚴，恐違上天垂戒之意，累兩宮好生之德。

translations.literal: Yet the edict-imposed prison has not been released, interrogation is still severe—I fear this violates Heaven's admonitory intent and burdens the virtue of compassion of both palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the special investigation continues, interrogation remains harsh, and I fear this runs counter to Heaven's warning and tarnishes the compassionate virtue of both palaces.

sentences.zh: 且婦人柔弱，箠楚之下，何求不可，萬一懷冤，足累和氣。

translations.literal: Moreover women are frail; under the rod and staff what confession could not be obtained—if by chance they harbor injustice, it is enough to harm harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Women are frail by nature; under the lash they will confess to anything. Should innocent persons be wronged, the harm to public harmony would be grave.

sentences.zh: 祥符中，宮掖火，先帝嘗索其類置之法矣，若防患以刑而止，豈復有今日之虞哉。

translations.literal: In the Xiangfu era there was palace fire; the former emperor once sought such cases and imposed law on them—if one stops at preventing disaster through punishment alone, how could there again be today's worry?
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiangfu era the palace also caught fire, and the late emperor sought out those responsible and punished them. If punishment alone could prevent such disasters, would we face this danger again today?

sentences.zh: 況變警之來，近在禁掖，誠願修政以禳之，思患以防之。

translations.literal: Moreover this warning of change has come close within the forbidden quarters; I sincerely wish to reform government to expel it and think of calamity to guard against it.
translations.idiomatic: This warning has come to the very heart of the palace. I earnestly pray that Your Majesty will reform governance to avert calamity and reflect on danger to guard against it.

sentences.zh: 凡逮繫者特從原免，庶災變可銷而福祥來格也。」

translations.literal: All those detained should be specially pardoned and released, so that perhaps calamitous change may be dispelled and fortune and auspice may come."
translations.idiomatic: All those detained should be specially pardoned and released, so that calamity may be dispelled and fortune and blessing may descend."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，仁宗為罷詔獄。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Renzong for this reason abolished the edict prison.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Renzong abolished the special investigation on that account.

sentences.zh: 時章獻太后猶臨朝，宗諒言國家以火德王，天下火失其性由政失其本，因請太后還政，而越亦上疏。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Dowager Zhangxian still held court; Zongliang said the state takes Fire as its virtue to rule, that fire throughout the realm loses its nature because government loses its root, and therefore requested the empress dowager return government; Yue also submitted a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager Zhangxian still held court at the time. Zongliang argued that the Song ruled by the virtue of Fire, that fire throughout the realm had lost its proper nature because government had lost its foundation, and petitioned the empress dowager to return power to the emperor; Liu Yue submitted a similar memorial.

sentences.zh: 太后崩，擢嘗言還政者，越已卒，贈右司諫，而除宗諒左正言。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, those who had spoken of returning government were promoted; Yue had already died and was posthumously given Right Secretariat Remonstrance; Zongliang was appointed Left Rectifier of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager's death, those who had urged the return of power were promoted. Yue had already died and was posthumously given the title Right Secretariat Remonstrance, while Zongliang was appointed Left Rectifier of Writings.

sentences.zh: 劉越者字子長，大名人。

translations.literal: Liu Yue's courtesy name was Zichang; he was a man of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yue, whose courtesy name was Zichang, was a native of Daming.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，有學行，亦宗諒同年進士。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned and poor, had learning and conduct, and was also a jinshi graduate in the same year as Zongliang.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, he was a man of learning and integrity and had passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Zongliang.

sentences.zh: 嘗知襄城、固始二縣，有能名。

translations.literal: He once was magistrate of Xiangcheng and Gushi counties and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He had served as magistrate of Xiangcheng and Gushi counties and earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 既贈官，又官其一子，賜其家錢十萬。

translations.literal: After the posthumous office was granted, one of his sons was also given an office, and his family was granted one hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: In addition to the posthumous title, one of his sons was given an official appointment and his family was granted one hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 宗諒後遷左司諫，坐言宮禁事不實，降尚書祠部員外郎、知信州。

translations.literal: Zongliang was later promoted to Left Secretariat Remonstrance; because statements on palace forbidden matters were not true he was demoted to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Sacrifices Section and made prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zongliang was later promoted to Left Secretariat Remonstrance but was demoted for making untrue statements about palace affairs to Outer Gentleman in the Sacrifices Section of the Ministry of Rites and prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 與范諷雅相善，及諷貶，宗諒降監池州酒。

translations.literal: He was on cordial terms with Fan Feng; when Feng was demoted, Zongliang was demoted to supervise Chizhou wine.
translations.idiomatic: He was on friendly terms with Fan Feng; when Feng was demoted, Zongliang was demoted to supervisor of wine production at Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，通判江寧府，徙知湖州。

translations.literal: After some time, he served as vice-prefect of Jiangning Prefecture, then was transferred to serve as prefect of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later he was made vice-prefect of Jiangning Prefecture, then transferred to serve as prefect of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 元昊反，除刑部員外郎、直集賢院、知涇州。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao rebelled, he was appointed Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Punishments, given direct appointment at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and made prefect of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao rebelled, he was appointed Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Punishments with direct appointment at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and made prefect of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 葛懷敏軍敗於定州，諸郡震恐，宗諒顧城中兵少，乃集農民數千戎服乘城，又募勇敢，諜知寇遠近及其形勢，檄報旁郡使為備。

translations.literal: Ge Huaimin's army was defeated at Dingzhou, and the neighboring prefectures were shaken with fear. Zongliang, seeing that troops in the city were few, gathered several thousand farmers in military dress to man the walls; he also recruited the bold, sent spies to learn the enemy's distance and disposition, and dispatched proclamations to neighboring prefectures urging them to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: After Ge Huaimin's army was defeated at Dingzhou, neighboring prefectures were gripped by fear. Seeing how few soldiers he had in the city, Zongliang mustered several thousand farmers in military dress to defend the walls, recruited brave men, sent scouts to learn how near the enemy was and in what strength, and notified neighboring prefectures by dispatch so they could ready their defenses.

sentences.zh: 會范仲淹自環慶引蕃漢兵來援，時天陰晦十餘日，人情憂沮，宗諒乃大設牛酒迎犒士卒；

translations.literal: It happened that Fan Zhongyan led Tangut and Han troops from Huanqing in relief; at the time the sky had been overcast and gloomy for more than ten days, and people's spirits were anxious and dejected, so Zongliang set out beef and wine on a grand scale to welcome and reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan then arrived from Huanqing with a combined force of Tangut and Han troops. The sky had been dark and overcast for more than ten days, morale was sinking, and Zongliang laid out a great feast of beef and wine to welcome and reward the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 又籍定州戰沒者於佛寺祭酹之，厚撫其孥，使各得所，於是邊民稍安。

translations.literal: He also registered those who had fallen in battle at Dingzhou and offered libations to them at a Buddhist temple, generously comforted their wives and children and saw that each found a place, and thereby the frontier people were somewhat reassured.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled a roll of those killed in battle at Dingzhou and performed memorial rites for them at a Buddhist temple, gave generous support to their families, and saw that they were provided for, so that the people on the frontier gradually regained their peace of mind.

sentences.zh: 仲淹薦以自代，擢天章閣待制，徙慶州。

translations.literal: Zhongyan recommended him to succeed himself; he was promoted to Attendant at the Tianzhang Pavilion and transferred to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan recommended him as his own successor; he was promoted to Attendant at the Tianzhang Pavilion and transferred to serve as prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 上言：「朝廷既授范仲淹、韓琦四路馬步軍都總管、經略安撫招討使，而諸路亦帶招討稱號，非所宜。」

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying, "The court has already appointed Fan Zhongyan and Han Qi as overall commanders of cavalry and infantry and as commissioners for pacification, comfort, and punitive campaigns over the four circuits, yet the various circuits also carry the title of punitive commissioner, which is not fitting."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne: "The court has already made Fan Zhongyan and Han Qi overall commanders of cavalry and infantry and commissioners for pacification, comfort, and punitive campaigns over the four frontier circuits. It is inappropriate for the other circuits to carry the punitive commissioner title as well."

sentences.zh: 詔罷之。

translations.literal: An edict abolished them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the titles abolished.

sentences.zh: 御史梁堅劾奏宗諒前在涇州費公錢十六萬貫，及遣中使檢視，乃始至部，日以故事犒賚諸部屬羌，又間以饋遺遊士故人。

translations.literal: Censor Liang Jian impeached Zongliang, charging that while previously at Jingzhou he had spent one hundred sixty thousand strings of public cash; when an imperial envoy was sent to inspect, it was found he had only just arrived at his post, yet day by day, according to precedent, he rewarded and bestowed gifts on the various subordinate Tangut tribes, and from time to time also sent presents to traveling scholars and old acquaintances.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liang Jian impeached Zongliang for having spent one hundred sixty thousand strings of public funds while at Jingzhou. When an imperial envoy was dispatched to investigate, it turned out he had only just taken up his post, yet he was already spending every day, by established custom, on rewards for the various subordinate Tangut tribes, and intermittently sending gifts to itinerant scholars and old friends.

sentences.zh: 宗諒恐連逮者眾，因焚其籍以滅姓名。

translations.literal: Zongliang feared that many would be implicated, and therefore burned the registers to erase the names.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that many people would be dragged into the case, Zongliang burned the account books to destroy the names.

sentences.zh: 仲淹時參知政事，力救之，止降一官，知虢州。

translations.literal: Zhongyan was then Vice Grand Councillor and exerted himself to save him; he was only demoted one rank and made prefect of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan, who was then Vice Grand Councillor, intervened strenuously on his behalf, and the penalty was reduced to a single demotion; he was made prefect of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王拱辰論奏不已，復徙岳州，稍遷蘇州，卒。

translations.literal: Imperial Censor Wang Gongchen continued submitting critiques without cease; Zongliang was again transferred to Yuezhou, was gradually moved to Suzhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Censor Wang Gongchen kept up his attacks without letup, and Zongliang was transferred again to Yuezhou, later moved to Suzhou, and there he died.

sentences.zh: 宗諒尚氣，倜儻自任，好施與，及卒，無餘財。

translations.literal: Zongliang was proud of spirit, free and self-reliant, and fond of giving; when he died he left no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Zongliang was proud and high-spirited, unconventional and self-assured, and generous to a fault; when he died he had nothing left.

sentences.zh: 所蒞州喜建學，而湖州最盛，學者傾江、淮間。

translations.literal: In every prefecture he governed he liked to establish schools, and Huzhou's was the most flourishing; scholars flocked from throughout the Jiang and Huai regions.
translations.idiomatic: In every prefecture he governed he took pleasure in founding schools; the one at Huzhou was the grandest, and scholars came from all across the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 有諫疏二十餘篇。

translations.literal: He left more than twenty remonstrance memorials.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty of his remonstrance memorials survive.

sentences.zh: 李防，字智周，大名內黃人。

translations.literal: Li Fang, courtesy name Zhizhou, was a man of Neihuang in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang, whose courtesy name was Zhizhou, was a native of Neihuang in Daming.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為莫州軍事推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and became military staff officer of Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he served as military staff officer of Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 隨曹彬入契丹，授忠武軍節度推官。

translations.literal: He followed Cao Bin into Khitan territory and was appointed staff officer of the Zhongwu Army circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Cao Bin on campaign into Khitan territory and was appointed staff officer to the Zhongwu Army circuit commissioner.

sentences.zh: 括磁、相二州逃戶田，增租賦十餘萬。

translations.literal: He surveyed the fields of absconding households in the Ci and Xiang prefectures and increased rent and tax by more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He surveyed land held by absconding households in Ci and Xiang prefectures and increased rent and tax receipts by more than one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 因請均定田稅，又請縣有破逃五十戶者，令、佐降下考，百戶殿三選，二百戶停所居官，能招攜者旌賞之。

translations.literal: Accordingly he requested equalization of field taxes, and also requested that in any county where absconding households reached fifty, the magistrate and assistant receive a lower evaluation; at one hundred households they be ranked last for three selection cycles; at two hundred households they be removed from office; and those able to induce people to return be commended and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: He then petitioned for a uniform assessment of field taxes and proposed that any county losing fifty households to flight should earn its magistrate and assistant a poor performance rating; at one hundred such households they should be ranked last for three promotion cycles; at two hundred they should be removed from office; and officials who succeeded in bringing people back should be commended and rewarded.

sentences.zh: 改秘書省著作佐郎、通判潞州，遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: He was changed to Collator of the Secretariat and vice-prefect of Luzhou, then promoted to Secretariat Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Collator of the Secretariat and vice-prefect of Luzhou, then promoted to Secretariat Assistant.

sentences.zh: 體量二浙民饑，建言逃戶田宜即召人耕種，使人不敢輕去川畝，而官賦常在。

translations.literal: Assessing famine among the people of the Two Zhes, he proposed that fields of absconding households should immediately be assigned for cultivation so that people would not lightly abandon their farmlands and official levies would remain steady.
translations.idiomatic: While assessing famine in the Two Zhe circuits, he proposed that abandoned fields be immediately put under cultivation so that people would not so readily leave their land and tax revenues would remain stable.

sentences.zh: 又請京師置折中倉，聽人入粟，以江、浙、荊湖物償之。

translations.literal: He also requested that a buffer granary be established in the capital, allowing people to deliver grain and be compensated with goods from Jiang-Zhe and Jing-Hu.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed establishing a buffer granary in the capital where grain could be delivered in exchange for goods from the Jiang-Zhe and Jing-Hu regions.

sentences.zh: 擢開封府推官，請與判官間三五日即府司軍巡院察冤獄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to investigating officer of Kaifeng Prefecture and requested that he and the administrative judge every few days inspect the military patrol court of the prefectural office for cases of injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to investigating officer of Kaifeng Prefecture, he asked that he and the administrative judge inspect the military patrol court every few days for wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 出為陝路轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as deputy transport commissioner of the Shaan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed deputy transport commissioner of the Shaan circuit.

sentences.zh: 先是沿江水遞，歲役民丁甚眾，頗廢農作，防悉以城卒代之。

translations.literal: Previously, along the Yangzi the courier service each year conscripted very many civilian laborers and greatly disrupted farming; Fang replaced them all with garrison soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Yangzi river courier service had conscripted large numbers of civilians each year, seriously disrupting agriculture; Fang replaced all of them with garrison soldiers.

sentences.zh: 會分川、陝為四路，徙防梓州路轉運使，累遷尚書工部員外郎，為三司戶部判官。

translations.literal: When Sichuan and Shaan were divided into four circuits, Fang was transferred to transport commissioner of the Zizhou circuit, was repeatedly promoted to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat, and served as Household Section judge of the State Finance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichuan and Shaan were reorganized into four circuits, Fang was made transport commissioner of the Zizhou circuit, rose through several promotions to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works, and served as judge of the Household Section of the State Finance Commission.

sentences.zh: 景德初，江南旱，詔與張知白分東、西路安撫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingde era, Jiangnan suffered drought; an edict ordered him and Zhang Zhibai to pacify the eastern and western routes separately.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era, when drought struck Jiangnan, he and Zhang Zhibai were ordered to undertake separate pacification missions along the eastern and western routes.

sentences.zh: 上言：「秦羲嘗增江、淮、兩浙、荊湖榷酤錢，民頗煩擾。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying, "Qin Xi once increased the liquor monopoly levies in the Jiang, Huai, Two Zhes, and Jing-Hu regions, and the people were greatly troubled.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne: "Qin Xi had once raised liquor monopoly taxes in the Jiang, Huai, Two Zhes, and Jing-Hu regions, causing considerable hardship among the people.

sentences.zh: 江南以歲饑權罷，而淮南、荊湖未被德音。」

translations.literal: Jiangnan had temporarily suspended them because of famine that year, yet Huainan and Jing-Hu had not received the gracious edict."
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan had temporarily suspended the increases because of that year's famine, but Huainan and Jing-Hu had received no comparable relief."

sentences.zh: 詔悉罷之，仍詔羲等毋得復增榷酤之利。

translations.literal: An edict abolished them all, and further ordered that Qin Xi and the others must not again increase liquor monopoly profits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished the increases entirely and further forbade Qin Xi and his associates from raising liquor monopoly revenues again.

sentences.zh: 遂為江南轉運。

translations.literal: He then became transport commissioner of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed transport commissioner of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 淮南舊不禁鹽，制置司請禁鹽而官自鬻之，使兵夫輦載江上，且多漂失之患。

translations.literal: Huainan had formerly not prohibited salt; the administrative commission requested prohibition of salt and that the government sell it itself, employing soldiers and laborers to haul it along the river, and there was moreover much loss from drifting and sinking.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan had not previously restricted salt trade, but the administrative commission proposed banning private salt and selling it through government monopoly, using soldiers and laborers to transport it along the river—a scheme plagued by losses from drifting and sinking.

sentences.zh: 防請令商人入錢帛京師，或輸芻糧西北邊，而給以鹽，則公私皆利，後采用之。

translations.literal: Fang requested that merchants be allowed to deliver cash and silk in the capital, or to supply fodder and grain to the northwest frontier, and in return be given salt; then both public and private interests would benefit. This was later adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Fang proposed letting merchants deliver cash and silk to the capital, or supply fodder and grain to the northwest frontier, in exchange for salt vouchers—a plan that would benefit both state and merchants. The proposal was later adopted.

sentences.zh: 徙知應天府，鑿府西障口為斗門，泄汴水，淤旁田數百畝，民甚利之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Yingtian Prefecture, cut a sluice gate at Zhangkou west of the prefectural seat to release Bian River water, and silted several hundred mu of neighboring fields; the people greatly benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Yingtian Prefecture, he cut a sluice gate at Zhangkou west of the city to channel Bian River water onto several hundred mu of neighboring fields, greatly benefiting the local people.

sentences.zh: 又徙興元府，入為三司鹽鐵判官，失舉免官。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Xingyuan Prefecture, entered service as Salt and Iron judge of the State Finance Commission, and was dismissed from office for a failed recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: He was next transferred to Xingyuan Prefecture, then recalled to serve as Salt and Iron judge of the State Finance Commission, but was dismissed after a faulty personnel recommendation.

sentences.zh: 後起通判河南府，徙知宿、延、亳三州，為利州路轉運使，累遷兵部郎中、糾察刑獄，擢右諫議大夫、知永興軍，進給事中，復知延州，更耀、潞二州，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was reappointed vice-prefect of Henan Prefecture, transferred to serve as prefect of Su, Yan, and Bo prefectures, became transport commissioner of the Lizhou circuit, was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Ministry of War and inspector of criminal cases, was elevated to Right Remonstrance Grandee and made military commissioner of Yongxing, advanced to Supervising Censor, again served as prefect of Yanzhou, was moved through Yao and Lu prefectures, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reinstated as vice-prefect of Henan Prefecture, then served successively as prefect of Su, Yan, and Bo prefectures and as transport commissioner of the Lizhou circuit. After several promotions he became Director of the Ministry of War and inspector of criminal cases, was elevated to Right Remonstrance Grandee and military commissioner of Yongxing, advanced to Supervising Censor, served again as prefect of Yanzhou, held Yao and Lu prefectures in turn, and died.

sentences.zh: 防好建明利害，所至必有論奏，朝廷頗施行之。

translations.literal: Fang liked to clarify benefits and harms; wherever he went he invariably submitted memorials, and the court often implemented them.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had a gift for articulating what would help and what would harm the state; wherever he served he submitted memorials, and the court frequently acted on his proposals.

sentences.zh: 其精力過人。

translations.literal: His energy surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: His energy and drive were extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 防在江南，晏殊以童子謁見，防命賦詩，使還薦之，後至宰相。

translations.literal: When Fang was in Jiangnan, Yan Shu came to see him as a child prodigy; Fang ordered him to compose a poem and, when he returned, recommended him; he later rose to Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: While Fang was serving in Jiangnan, the child prodigy Yan Shu came to call on him. Fang asked him to compose a poem and, impressed, recommended him on his return; Yan Shu later rose to Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 趙湘，字巨源，華州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Xiang, courtesy name Juyuan, was a man of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiang, whose courtesy name was Juyuan, was a native of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 進士甲科，歷彰武、永興、昭武三軍節度推官，遷秘書省著作佐郎、知新繁縣。

translations.literal: He graduated jinshi in the top class, served successively as staff officer to the commissioners of the Zhangwu, Yongxing, and Zhaowu armies, and was promoted to Collator of the Secretariat and magistrate of Xinfan County.
translations.idiomatic: Graduating jinshi in the top class, he served as staff officer to the commissioners of the Zhangwu, Yongxing, and Zhaowu armies in turn, then was promoted to Collator of the Secretariat and appointed magistrate of Xinfan County.

sentences.zh: 以吏最，命知商州，徙隴州、興元府，再遷太常博士。

translations.literal: For excellence in administration he was appointed prefect of Shangzhou, transferred to Longzhou and Xingyuan Prefecture, and was again promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Rated highest for administrative performance, he was made prefect of Shangzhou, transferred to Longzhou and Xingyuan Prefecture, and was then promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 上《補政忠言》十篇，召判宗正寺，賜白金二百兩。

translations.literal: He submitted ten chapters of "Faithful Words to Supplement Governance," was summoned to serve as administrative judge of the Court of the Imperial Clan, and was granted two hundred taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted ten chapters of Faithful Words to Supplement Governance, was summoned to serve as administrative judge of the Court of the Imperial Clan, and was granted two hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 久之，上書言：「元德李太后母育聖躬，請祔太宗廟室。」

translations.literal: After some time he submitted a memorial saying, "Empress Dowager Yuande, the Li consort, nourished and raised the sacred person; I request that she be enshrined in Emperor Taizong's temple chamber."
translations.idiomatic: Some time later he submitted a memorial saying, "Empress Dowager Yuande of the Li clan had raised the emperor from infancy and should be enshrined in Emperor Taizong's temple."

sentences.zh: 後用其說。

translations.literal: Later his proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: His proposal was later adopted.

sentences.zh: 冊趙德明，假尚書禮部員外郎，為官告副使。

translations.literal: When Zhao Deming was enfeoffed, he was given acting appointment as Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites and served as deputy envoy for the patent of office.
translations.idiomatic: At the enfeoffment of Zhao Deming, he served as acting Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites and deputy envoy presenting the patent of office.

sentences.zh: 擢殿中侍御史，權判三司勾院，上言：「漢章帝以《月令》冬至之後有順陽助生之文，而無鞫獄斷刑之政，遂定令毋以十一月、十二月報囚。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Censor and given provisional charge of the State Finance Commission audit office. He submitted a memorial saying, "Emperor Zhang of Han, because the Monthly Ordinances after the winter solstice contain language on compliant yang assisting life, and contain no policy of trying cases and passing sentence, established the rule that capital cases not be reported in the eleventh and twelfth months.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Palace Censor with provisional charge of the State Finance Commission audit office, he memorialized: "Emperor Zhang of Han noted that the Monthly Ordinances after the winter solstice speak of compliant yang nurturing life and say nothing about trying cases and passing sentence, and therefore decreed that capital cases not be reported in the eleventh and twelfth months.

sentences.zh: 今季冬誕聖之月而決大辟不廢。

translations.literal: Now, in the winter month of the emperor's birth, the practice of executing those condemned to death is not suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Yet today, even in the winter month marking the emperor's birth, executions of those condemned to death continue unabated.

sentences.zh: 願詔有司，自仲冬留大辟弗決，俟孟春臨軒閱視，情可矜惻者貸之，他論如法。」

translations.literal: I wish that an edict be issued to the responsible offices that from mid-winter capital cases be held undecided, and that when the emperor reviews them at the palace in early spring, those whose circumstances merit compassion be pardoned, while all others be judged according to law."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the responsible offices be ordered to withhold final judgment on capital cases from mid-winter onward, and that when the emperor reviews them at court in early spring, those whose circumstances warrant mercy be pardoned while all others be sentenced according to law."

sentences.zh: 真宗曰：「此固善矣，然慮繫囚益淹久，吏或因緣為奸爾。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong said, "This is indeed good, yet I fear that prisoners under detention would be detained all the longer, and clerks might take advantage of the delay to commit abuses."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong replied, "That would indeed be admirable, but I worry that prisoners would languish in custody even longer and that officials might exploit the delay for corrupt purposes."

sentences.zh: 湘又上書請封禪。

translations.literal: Xiang again submitted a memorial requesting the feng and shan rites.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang then submitted another memorial requesting the feng and shan sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 未幾，命管勾南宮北宅事。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered to manage affairs of the Southern and Northern Palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed to oversee affairs of the Southern and Northern Palaces.

sentences.zh: 東封泰山，為東京留守推官，禮成，遷侍御史。

translations.literal: When the eastern feng rite was performed at Mount Tai, he served as staff investigating officer for the eastern capital stay-behind administration; when the rites were completed he was promoted to Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the eastern feng ceremony at Mount Tai he served as investigating officer for the eastern capital stay-behind administration; after the rites were completed he was promoted to Censor.

sentences.zh: 昇州火，命湘往致祠，兼問民疾苦。

translations.literal: When fire broke out in Shengzhou, Xiang was ordered to go perform sacrificial rites and also inquire into the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: When fire struck Shengzhou, Xiang was dispatched to perform sacrificial rites and to inquire into the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 還言轉運使劉炤弛職不按部，知洪州馬景病不任事，皆罷黜之。

translations.literal: On his return he reported that transport commissioner Liu Zhao was negligent in duty and did not tour his circuit, and that Ma Jing, prefect of Hongzhou, was ill and unfit for office; both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he reported that transport commissioner Liu Zhao had neglected his duties and failed to tour his circuit, and that Ma Jing, prefect of Hongzhou, was too ill to perform his duties; both were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 糾察刑獄，改尚書刑部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: He inspected criminal cases, was changed to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Punishments concurrently serving as Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed inspector of criminal cases, he was made Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Punishments while concurrently serving as Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs.

sentences.zh: 湘又言：「舊制文武常參官日趨朝，並赴待漏院俟禁門辟，今則辰漏上始放外朝，故朝者多後時乃入。

translations.literal: Xiang also said, "Under the old system, civil and military officials attending court daily all proceeded to the Awaiting-the-Gong courtyard to wait until the forbidden gate opened; now the outer court is not opened until the fifth watch of the morning, so many who attend court arrive late.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang also memorialized: "Under the old system, civil and military officials who attended court daily gathered in the Awaiting-the-Gong courtyard to wait for the palace gate to open. Now the outer court is not opened until the fifth watch, and many officials arrive late.

sentences.zh: 望敕正衙門主者察晚至，以懲其慢。

translations.literal: I hope an edict will instruct the gatekeepers of the main court to observe those who arrive late and punish their tardiness.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the gatekeepers of the main court be ordered to note late arrivals and punish such negligence.

sentences.zh: 若風雨寒暑託病不朝者罪之。」

translations.literal: Those who plead illness on account of wind, rain, cold, or heat and fail to attend court should be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Officials who feign illness to avoid court on account of weather should likewise be punished."

sentences.zh: 時帝親製五箴以自儆，湘因言：「宗室風化所本，宜有以訓厲，願特製銘以賜南北邸。」

translations.literal: At the time the emperor had personally composed five admonitions to warn himself. Xiang therefore said, "The imperial clan is the root of custom and transformation; they should be instructed and admonished. I wish that a special inscription be composed and bestowed on the southern and northern lodges."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had recently composed five admonitions for his own guidance. Xiang added: "The imperial clan is the foundation of public morals and ought to be instructed and admonished. I ask that a special inscription be composed and bestowed on the southern and northern clan lodges."

sentences.zh: 帝悅，為製宗室座右銘，賜寧王元偓以下並及湘，且諭之曰：「卿宗姓也，故賜卿。」

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, composed an inscription for the imperial clan to place beside their seats, and bestowed it on Prince of Ning Yuanwei and those below, and also on Xiang, telling him, "You bear the imperial surname; therefore I bestow it on you as well."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, composed an inscription for the imperial clan to keep at hand, and bestowed copies on Prince of Ning Yuanwei and the ranks below—and on Xiang as well, telling him, "You share the imperial surname, and so I grant this to you too."

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，為考制度副使，請如《周官》置土訓，錄所過州縣山川與俗好惡，日上奏御。

translations.literal: At the sacrifice at Fen-yin he served as deputy commissioner for examining ritual institutions, requested that territorial instructors be established as in the Offices of Zhou, recorded the mountains, rivers, and local customs and preferences of the prefectures and counties passed through, and submitted daily reports to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At the Fen-yin sacrifice he served as deputy commissioner for examining ritual institutions, proposed establishing territorial instructors as described in the Offices of Zhou, recorded the geography and local customs of each prefecture and county along the route, and submitted daily reports to the throne.

sentences.zh: 兼判宗正寺。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as administrative judge of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as administrative judge of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 歷三司戶部、度支副使。

translations.literal: He served successively as deputy commissioner of the Household and Expenditure sections of the State Finance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as deputy commissioner of the Household and Expenditure sections of the State Finance Commission.

sentences.zh: 祀太清宮，管勾留司三司事。

translations.literal: At the sacrifice at the Grand Pure Palace he managed affairs of the stay-behind State Finance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: During the sacrifice at the Grand Pure Palace he oversaw the stay-behind administration of the State Finance Commission.

sentences.zh: 為鹽鐵副使，再遷工部郎中、直昭文館，出知河南府，徙河中府，為京西轉運使。

translations.literal: He became deputy commissioner of Salt and Iron, was again promoted to Director of the Ministry of Works with direct appointment at the Hall of Broad Culture, was sent out as prefect of Henan Prefecture, transferred to Hezhong Prefecture, and served as transport commissioner of the Jingxi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became deputy commissioner of Salt and Iron, was promoted again to Director of the Ministry of Works with direct appointment at the Hall of Broad Culture, served as prefect of Henan Prefecture, was transferred to Hezhong Prefecture, and was appointed transport commissioner of the Jingxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 又徙鳳翔府、延州，遷太常少卿、知襄州。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Fengxiang Prefecture and Yanzhou, was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and served as prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to Fengxiang Prefecture and Yanzhou, promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and appointed prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又知應天府，進右諫議大夫，復知河南，為集賢院學士，以疾徙虢州，卒。

translations.literal: He again served as prefect of Yingtian Prefecture, advanced to Right Remonstrance Grandee, again served as prefect of Henan, became Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, was transferred to Guozhou because of illness, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served again as prefect of Yingtian Prefecture, was promoted to Right Remonstrance Grandee, returned as prefect of Henan, became Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, was transferred to Guozhou on account of illness, and died there.

sentences.zh: 唐肅，字叔元，杭州錢塘人。

translations.literal: Tang Su, courtesy name Shuyuan, was a man of Qiantang in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Su, whose courtesy name was Shuyuan, was a native of Qiantang in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 當錢俶時，始七歲，能誦《五經》，名聞其國中。

translations.literal: During the time of Qian Chu, when he was only seven, he could recite the Five Classics, and his fame spread throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qian Chu, while still only seven years old, he could recite the Five Classics, and his reputation spread throughout the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 後與孫何、丁謂、曹商遊，學者慕之。

translations.literal: Later he associated with Sun He, Ding Wei, and Cao Shang, and scholars admired them.
translations.idiomatic: He later kept company with Sun He, Ding Wei, and Cao Shang, and scholars looked up to the circle.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，調郿縣主簿，徙泰州司理參軍。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed chief clerk of Mei County, and was transferred to judicial administrator of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he was appointed chief clerk of Mei County and then transferred to serve as judicial administrator of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 有商人寓逆旅，而同宿者殺人亡去，商人夜聞人聲，往視之，血沾商人衣，為捕吏所執，州趣獄具。

translations.literal: A merchant lodged at an inn, and a fellow lodger killed someone and fled. The merchant heard voices in the night and went to look; blood stained the merchant's clothes, and he was seized by arresting officers. The prefecture pressed for a completed case.
translations.idiomatic: A merchant staying at an inn found that a fellow lodger had killed someone and fled. Hearing voices in the night, the merchant went to investigate; blood splattered his clothes, and the arresting officers took him into custody. The prefecture pressed for a quick conviction.

sentences.zh: 肅探知其冤，持之，後數日得殺人者。

translations.literal: Su investigated and learned of his injustice; he held to the case, and several days later the killer was found.
translations.idiomatic: Su investigated and found that the merchant had been wronged; he held firm against the rush to judgment, and within days the real killer was apprehended.

sentences.zh: 後守雷有終就辟為觀察推官。

translations.literal: Later, when Lei Youzhong served as prefect, Su was recruited as surveillance staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Lei Youzhong became prefect, he recruited Su as staff officer to the surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書省著作佐郎，歷知聞喜、福昌縣，通判陝州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Collator of the Secretariat, served successively as magistrate of Wenxi and Fuchang counties, and was vice-prefect of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Collator of the Secretariat, he served as magistrate of Wenxi and Fuchang counties in turn and as vice-prefect of Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 召拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital and appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 或薦肅為群牧判官，真宗曰：「朕欲別用肅。」

translations.literal: Someone recommended Su as judge of the Pasturage Commission, and Emperor Zhenzong said, "I wish to employ Su elsewhere."
translations.idiomatic: When someone recommended Su for judge of the Pasturage Commission, Emperor Zhenzong said, "I have another appointment in mind for Su."

sentences.zh: 遂提點梓州路刑獄。

translations.literal: He was therefore made judicial intendant of the Zizhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Su was accordingly appointed judicial intendant of the Zizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史，入為三司戶部判官，出知舒州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Censor, entered service as judge of the Household Section of the State Finance Commission, and was sent out as prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Palace Censor, he was recalled to serve as judge of the Household Section of the State Finance Commission, then sent out as prefect of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史，為福建路轉運使，判三司開拆司。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Censor, served as transport commissioner of the Fujian circuit, and was judge of the State Finance Commission's Unpacking Office.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Censor, he served as transport commissioner of the Fujian circuit and as judge of the State Finance Commission's Unpacking Office.

sentences.zh: 再遷工部郎中、知洪州。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Director of the Ministry of Works and made prefect of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Director of the Ministry of Works and appointed prefect of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋為江南東路轉運使，擢三司度支副使。

translations.literal: Soon he became transport commissioner of the Jiangnan East circuit and was elevated to deputy commissioner of the Expenditure Section of the State Finance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became transport commissioner of the Jiangnan East circuit and was elevated to deputy commissioner of the Expenditure Section of the State Finance Commission.

sentences.zh: 奉使契丹，還，遷刑部。

translations.literal: On an embassy to the Khitan he returned and was promoted within the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: After serving on an embassy to the Khitan, he returned and was promoted within the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 為龍圖閣待制、登聞檢院，知審刑院，卒。

translations.literal: He became Attendant at the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and inspector of the Petition Office, served as director of the Court for Review of Punishments, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He became Attendant at the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and inspector of the Petition Office, served as director of the Court for Review of Punishments, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子詢。

translations.literal: His son was Xun.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xun.

sentences.zh: 子 詢

translations.literal: Son: Xun
translations.idiomatic: His son, Xun

sentences.zh: 詢，字彥猷，以父任為將作監主簿。

translations.literal: Xun, courtesy name Yanyou, entered office through his father's privilege as chief clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, whose courtesy name was Yanyou, entered office by virtue of his father's rank as chief clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，詔許天下士獻文章，應詔者百數，有司第其善者，詢數人而已，詔賜進士及第、知長興縣。

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era, an edict permitted scholars throughout the realm to submit writings; those who responded numbered in the hundreds, and the responsible offices ranked the best—only a few including Xun—and an edict granted them jinshi status and made Xun magistrate of Changxing County.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng era, an edict invited scholars throughout the empire to submit writings. Several hundred responded; the responsible offices ranked the best submissions, and only a handful—including Xun—were chosen. An edict granted them jinshi status, and Xun was appointed magistrate of Changxing County.

sentences.zh: 後以太常博士知歸州，用翰林學士吳育薦為御史，未至，喪母。

translations.literal: Later, as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he served as prefect of Guizhou; on the recommendation of Hanlin Academician Wu Yu he was appointed censor, but before he arrived his mother died.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while serving as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Guizhou, he was recommended for censor by Hanlin Academician Wu Yu, but before he could take up the post his mother died.

sentences.zh: 服除，育方參政事，宰相賈昌朝與詢有親嫌，育數與昌朝言，詢用故事當罷御史，昌朝欲留詢，不得已，以知廬州。

translations.literal: When mourning was completed, Yu was then Vice Grand Councillor; Grand Councillor Jia Changchao had a family connection with Xun that created a conflict of interest. Yu repeatedly told Changchao that by precedent Xun should be removed from the censorate; Changchao wished to keep Xun but, having no choice, appointed him prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period, Wu Yu had become Vice Grand Councillor. Grand Councillor Jia Changchao was related to Xun by marriage, and Yu repeatedly argued that precedent required Xun to leave the censorate. Changchao wanted to keep him but, unable to do so, appointed him prefect of Luzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 凡官外徙者皆放朝辭，而詢獨不用，比入見，中丞張方平乃奏留詢，育爭不能得，詢由是怨育而附昌朝。

translations.literal: Generally officials transferred outside the capital were granted a farewell audience at court, yet Xun alone was not given one. When he came to take leave, Imperial Censor Zhang Fangping submitted a memorial to retain him; Yu disputed this but could not prevail, and Xun therefore resented Yu and attached himself to Changchao.
translations.idiomatic: Officials transferred out of the capital were normally granted a farewell audience, but Xun was denied one. When he came to bid farewell, Imperial Censor Zhang Fangping memorialized to keep him at court; Yu objected but could not prevail, and Xun thereafter resented Yu and aligned himself with Changchao.

sentences.zh: 昌朝雅不善育，詢希其旨上奏曰：「賢良方正、直言極諫、茂才異等科，漢、唐皆不常置。
