translations.literal: Changchao had never been on good terms with Yu; Xun, seeking to please him, submitted a memorial saying, "The categories of Worthy and Good, Direct Speech and Extreme Remonstrance, and Outstanding Talent and Exceptional Grade were not regularly established in Han and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Changchao had long disliked Wu Yu. Seeking to curry favor, Xun submitted a memorial saying, "The categories of Worthy and Good, Direct Speech and Extreme Remonstrance, and Outstanding Talent and Exceptional Grade had not been regularly established in Han and Tang times.

sentences.zh: 若天見災異，政有闕失，則詔在位薦之，不可與進士同時設科。

translations.literal: If Heaven displayed calamities and portents and government had failings, then an edict would instruct those in office to recommend candidates; they should not be established as an examination category at the same time as the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: They were summoned only when Heaven sent omens and government had failed, at which point officials in office were ordered to recommend candidates—not held concurrently with the regular jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 若因災異，非時舉擢，宜如漢故事，親策當世要務，罷秘閣之試。」

translations.literal: If selection were made because of calamities and portents as an extraordinary promotion, it should follow Han precedent: the emperor should personally examine candidates on the urgent affairs of the age, and the Palace Library examination should be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: If such candidates were to be selected in response to omens as an extraordinary measure, the Han precedent should be followed: the emperor should personally examine them on pressing affairs of state, and the Palace Library examination should be abolished."

sentences.zh: 育亦奏言：「三代以來，取士之盛，莫如漢、唐。

translations.literal: Yu also submitted a memorial saying, "From the Three Dynasties onward, in the flourishing of recruitment of scholars none matched Han and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yu countered with a memorial of his own: "From the Three Dynasties onward, no age matched Han and Tang in the breadth and vigor of recruiting talent.

sentences.zh: 漢詔舉賢良文學直言極諫之士，非有災異而舉。

translations.literal: Han edicts summoned Worthy and Good, Literary and Learned, and Direct Speech and Extreme Remonstrance scholars—not summoned because there were calamities and portents.
translations.idiomatic: The Han court regularly summoned men of worth, learning, and forthright remonstrance—not only when calamities appeared.

sentences.zh: 唐制科之盛，固不專於災異也。

translations.literal: The flourishing of Tang special examination categories likewise did not depend solely on calamities and portents.
translations.idiomatic: The flourishing of Tang special examination categories likewise did not depend solely on omens and disasters.

sentences.zh: 況災異之出，或彌年所無，則此舉奚設？

translations.literal: Moreover, when calamities and portents appear, years may pass without any; then of what use would this measure be?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, calamities and portents may not appear for years on end—so what would be the point of such a policy?

sentences.zh: 或頻歲而有，則於事太煩。

translations.literal: Or if they occur in consecutive years, then the affair would be too burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: If examinations were held every year or two, the burden on the administration would be excessive.

sentences.zh: 令禮部進士數年一舉，因以製科隨之，則事與時宜。

translations.literal: Order the Ministry of Rites to hold the jinshi examination once every few years, and have the special examination follow accordingly—then the matter would suit the times.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Ministry of Rites hold the jinshi examination every few years and attach the special examination to that cycle, and the arrangement would suit the times.

sentences.zh: 又從而更張之，使遺材絕望，非所以廣賢路也。」

translations.literal: Again to change it further would make overlooked talent despair—it is not the way to broaden the path for the worthy."
translations.idiomatic: To change the system yet again would only leave overlooked talent in despair—it is no way to widen the road by which the worthy enter service."

sentences.zh: 仁宗是育言，詔禮部：「自今制科隨進士貢舉，其著為令。」

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong approved Yu's words and issued an edict the Ministry of Rites: "From now on the special examination shall follow the jinshi tribute selection; let this be established as regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong accepted Yu's argument and ordered the Ministry of Rites: "Henceforth the special examination shall follow the jinshi selection cycle. Establish this as permanent regulation."

sentences.zh: 時育由制科進，帝以為得人，故詢力肆排詆，意在育不在制科也。

translations.literal: At that time Yu had advanced through the special examination, and the Emperor considered it a good appointment. Therefore Xun exerted himself to slander him without restraint—his intent was directed at Yu, not at the special examination itself.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had risen through the special examination, and the Emperor regarded him as a worthy appointment. Xun therefore attacked him relentlessly; his target was Yu himself, not the special examination.

sentences.zh: 育弟婦故駙馬都尉李遵勖妹，有六子而寡。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother's wife was formerly the sister of Li Zunxu, Commandant-Attendant of the Imperial Son-in-Law; she had six sons and was a widow.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's sister-in-law was the sister of Li Zunxu, a former imperial son-in-law; she had borne six sons and was now a widow.

sentences.zh: 詢又奏育弟婦久寡不使更嫁，欲用此附李氏自進。

translations.literal: Xun again memorialized that Yu's sister-in-law had long been a widow without being permitted to remarry, intending to use this to attach himself to the Li clan and advance himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xun memorialized again that Yu's sister-in-law had long been kept from remarrying, hoping to use the charge to ingratiate himself with the Li family and advance his own career.

sentences.zh: 後詢終以故事罷御史，除尚書工部員外郎、直史館、知湖州，徙江西轉運使。

translations.literal: Later Xun was finally dismissed as censor on grounds of precedent, appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat, concurrently at the Historiography Institute, and prefect of Huzhou; then transferred as transport commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was eventually removed from the censorate on grounds of precedent, appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Works with a concurrent post at the Historiography Institute, made prefect of Huzhou, and then transferred to transport commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 會詔淮南、江、浙、荊湖六路轉運司移文發運使如所屬，詢爭以為不可，乃移福建路。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered the six circuits of Huainan, Jiang, Zhe, and Jinghu transport offices to issue documents to grain transport commissioners as to subordinates, Xun contended that this was improper, and was transferred to Fujian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict directed the transport offices of the six Huainan, Jiang, Zhe, and Jinghu circuits to treat grain transport commissioners as subordinates in official correspondence, Xun protested that this was improper and was reassigned to Fujian Circuit.

sentences.zh: 還，為三司戶部判官，又判磨勘司，出為江東轉運使。

translations.literal: Upon return, he served as judicial intendant of the Household Bureau of the Three Departments, also serving in the Audit Bureau, then went out as transport commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he served as judicial intendant of the Three Departments' Household Bureau and of the Audit Bureau, then was posted as transport commissioner of Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 上言：「執政純取科名顯者修起居注，非故事。」

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial: "The chief ministers exclusively selected those with prominent examination titles to compile the Daily Record—this is not precedent."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "The chief ministers have been appointing only men with famous examination credentials to compile the Daily Record. That is not established practice."

sentences.zh: 未幾，起居注闕人，帝特用詢，遂知制誥。

translations.literal: Before long the Daily Record had a vacancy, and the Emperor specially selected Xun; he then became drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a vacancy opened on the Daily Record staff, and the Emperor personally chose Xun for the post, after which he became a drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 以參知政事曾公亮親嫌，出知蘇州，徙杭、青二州，進翰林侍讀學士，累遷右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Because of kinship with the Associate Administrator Zeng Gongliang, he was sent out as prefect of Suzhou, transferred to Hang and Qing prefectures, promoted to Hanlin Attendant Reader, and incrementally promoted to Right Remonstrance Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Because of a kinship conflict with Associate Administrator Zeng Gongliang, he was sent out as prefect of Suzhou, then transferred to Hang and Qing prefectures, promoted to Hanlin Attendant Reader, and eventually rose to Right Remonstrance Counselor.

sentences.zh: 召還，勾當三班院，判太常寺，進給事中，卒，贈禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Recalled, he supervised the Three-Rank Bureau, served as judicial intendant of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted to Supervising Censor, died, posthumously enfeoffed as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he supervised the Three-Rank Bureau and served as judicial intendant of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was promoted to Supervising Censor, and died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 有集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 詢少刻勵自修，已而不固所守，及知湖州，悅官妓取以為妾。

translations.literal: Xun in youth was industrious in self-cultivation, but later did not hold firm to what he had guarded; when he became prefect of Huzhou, he took a liking to a courtesan and took her as concubine.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Xun was diligent in self-cultivation, but later he abandoned the standards he had upheld; when he became prefect of Huzhou, he took a fancy to a government courtesan and made her his concubine.

sentences.zh: 好畜硯，客至輒出而玩之，有《硯錄》三卷。

translations.literal: He loved collecting inkstones; when guests arrived he would always bring them out to admire them. He had Inkstone Records in three juan.
translations.idiomatic: He loved collecting inkstones and would bring them out whenever guests arrived to admire them together. He wrote Inkstone Records in three juan.

sentences.zh: 子坰，附王安石為監察御史裏行，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Jiong attached himself to Wang Anshi as a censor-in-attendance, and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiong aligned himself with Wang Anshi and served as a censor-in-attendance; he has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宋承平日久，吏多以嚴刻為治。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Song had long enjoyed peace, and officials often took severity as their mode of governance.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: The Song had long known peace, and officials often governed through harsh severity.

sentences.zh: 昷之辨冤獄，配奸吏；

translations.literal: Wen Zhi distinguished wrongful cases and banished corrupt clerks;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhi cleared wrongful convictions and banished corrupt clerks;

sentences.zh: 瓘奏還婦女為傭者若干人；

translations.literal: Guan memorialized to restore to freedom several women enslaved as laborers;
translations.idiomatic: Guan memorialized for the release of several women forced into servitude;

sentences.zh: 琰吏事不下於瓘，脫械縱囚，審知奸弊，何其明且決也。

translations.literal: Yan was no lesser than Guan in administrative matters—releasing shackles and freeing prisoners, yet discerning corruption and malfeasance: how bright and decisive!
translations.idiomatic: Yan was Guan's equal in administrative skill—he would remove shackles and release prisoners, yet still expose corruption and abuse. How clear-eyed and resolute he was!

sentences.zh: 宗諒、劉越以孤生立朝，請太后還政。

translations.literal: Zongliang and Liu Yue, as lone scholars standing at court, petitioned the Empress Dowager to return power.
translations.idiomatic: Zongliang and Liu Yue, men of humble origin who had risen at court, petitioned the Empress Dowager to restore the emperor's authority.

sentences.zh: 越年不逮用，聲名與宗諒同矣。

translations.literal: Yue's years did not reach full employment, yet his fame equaled Zongliang's.
translations.idiomatic: Yue did not live to see his full potential realized, yet his reputation stood equal to Zongliang's.

sentences.zh: 防請罷榷酤，興水利，湘廉問疾苦，按不稱職者；

translations.literal: Fang petitioned to abolish the liquor monopoly, develop waterworks, and as Xiang's inspector inquired into the people's suffering and investigated the unfit;
translations.idiomatic: Fang petitioned to abolish the liquor monopoly and develop irrigation works; as inspector of Xiang he inquired into popular hardship and investigated incompetent officials;

sentences.zh: 肅明於獄訟：皆不多見也。

translations.literal: Su was clear-minded in prison litigation—all these were not often seen.
translations.idiomatic: Su was clear-minded in criminal cases—all such examples were rare.

sentences.zh: 然昷之以殺降而奪官，瓘以能置對而興謗，詢傅會喜進，竊非其據，雖列侍從，君子所不與也。

translations.literal: Yet Wen Zhi lost his office for killing surrendering troops; Guan stirred slander for his skill at court responses; Xun opportunistically ingratiated himself for advancement—the grounds for each were questionable; though they ranked among attendants, gentlemen would not associate with them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wen Zhi was stripped of office for killing surrendered troops; Guan provoked slander through his skill at court debate; Xun curried favor and sought advancement by opportunistic means—the grounds for each were dubious. Though they held posts among the emperor's attendants, gentlemen would not count them as their own.

sentences.zh: 張述，字紹明，遂州小溪人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shu, styled Shaoming, a native of Xiaoxi in Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shu, styled Shaoming, was a native of Xiaoxi in Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，調咸陽縣主簿，改大理寺丞，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: Passed the jinshi examination, appointed registrar of Xianyang County, changed to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review, promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed registrar of Xianyang County, transferred to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review, and promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，仁宗未有嗣，述上書曰：「生民之命，繫於宗廟社稷，而繼嗣為之本。

translations.literal: In the Huangyou era, Emperor Renzong had no heir; Shu submitted a memorial saying: "The people's lives depend on the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain, and succession is the foundation of this.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangyou era, Emperor Renzong still had no heir. Shu submitted a memorial: "The fate of the people rests on the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain, and succession is the foundation of both.

sentences.zh: 匹夫有百金之產，猶能定謀託後，事出於素，況有天下者哉。

translations.literal: A common man with a hundred in gold property can still set plans and entrust posterity, the matter arising from what is ordinary—how much more one who possesses the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Even a common man with a modest estate of a hundred in gold can plan ahead and provide for posterity as a matter of course. How much more should one who holds the realm!

sentences.zh: 陛下承三聖之業，傳之千萬年，斯為孝矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty inherits the enterprise of the Three Sage Emperors and passes it on for ten thousand years—this is filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty inherits the legacy of the Three Sage Emperors and should pass it down for ten thousand generations. That would be true filial piety.

sentences.zh: 宗廟社稷未有託焉，此臣所以夙夜彷徨而為陛下憂也。

translations.literal: The ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain have no one entrusted to them—this is why your subject roams day and night in anxiety for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain have no heir entrusted to them. That is why your subject lies awake night after night in anxiety for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 謂宜慎擇宗親才而賢者，異其禮秩，試以職務，俾內外知聖心有所屬，則天下大幸。」

translations.literal: Your subject submits that one should carefully select from among the imperial clansmen those who are talented and worthy, distinguish their ritual rank, test them with official duties, so that within and without all would know where the sage heart is inclined—then the realm would be greatly blessed."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject submits that Your Majesty should carefully choose talented and worthy members of the imperial clan, distinguish them in rank and ceremony, and test them in office, so that court and country alike may know where the sage heart is set. That would be the realm's great good fortune."

sentences.zh: 至和元年，復上疏曰：「臣聞『明兩作離，大人以繼明照四方』。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhihe, he again submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard, 'When two brightnesses form Li, the great man uses succeeding brightness to illuminate the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhihe he submitted another memorial: "Your subject has read, 'When two suns form the hexagram Li, the great man uses successive illumination to light the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 離為日，君象也。

translations.literal: Li represents the sun—the image of the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Li stands for the sun, the symbol of the ruler.

sentences.zh: 二明相繼故能久照，東昇西沒，晝夜迭運，數之常也。

translations.literal: Two brightnesses succeeding one another can therefore shine long; the east rising and west setting, day and night alternating in motion—the regularity of number.
translations.idiomatic: Two suns succeeding one another can shine without end, as one rises in the east and sets in the west, day and night alternating in turn. Such is the constant order of things.

sentences.zh: 陛下御天下且三紀矣，是日之正中也，而未聞以繼照為慮，臣竊疑之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ruled the realm for nearly three reign periods—this is the sun at its zenith—yet I have not heard concern for succeeding illumination; your subject privately finds this doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has ruled the realm for nearly three decades—the sun at its zenith—yet I have heard no concern for who will succeed to the throne. Your subject finds this troubling.

sentences.zh: 歷觀前世或令出宮闈，或謀起閽寺，或奸臣首議，利幼主以專政，假後宮以盜權，安危之機發於頃刻。

translations.literal: Reviewing past ages: sometimes orders issued from the inner palace, sometimes plots arising from eunuch offices, sometimes villainous ministers initiating policy—profiting from a young lord to monopolize government, borrowing the rear palace to usurp power—the mechanism of safety and peril erupting in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back through history, one sees orders issued from the inner palace, plots hatched in the eunuch quarters, and villainous ministers taking the lead—exploiting a child emperor to seize power, or using the empress dowager's authority for private ends. The turn from safety to peril can come in an instant.

sentences.zh: 朝議恬然，曾不為計，此臣拳拳為陛下言也。」

translations.literal: Court deliberation remained at ease, never making plans—this is what your subject earnestly speaks to Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Yet court deliberation proceeds as if untroubled, with no plan in place. That is what your subject earnestly presses upon Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 述前後七上疏，最後語尤激，仁宗終不以為罪。

translations.literal: Shu submitted seven memorials in all; the language of the last was especially forceful, yet Renzong ultimately did not hold it against him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu submitted seven memorials in all; the last was especially forceful in tone, yet Emperor Renzong never treated it as an offense.

sentences.zh: 述慷慨喜論事，歷通判延州，知泗州，皆有政跡。

translations.literal: Shu was magnanimous and fond of discussing affairs; successively as supervising prefect of Yanzhou and prefect of Sizhou, he had administrative achievements in both.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was forthright and loved to discuss public affairs. As supervising prefect of Yanzhou and then prefect of Sizhou, he left a record of achievement in both posts.

sentences.zh: 後以尚書職方員外郎為江、浙、荊湖、福建、廣南路提點坑冶鐵錢事，行至萬州，道病卒。

translations.literal: Later, as Vice Director of the Bureau of Garrison Affairs in the Secretariat, he was commissioner for mining, smelting, and iron coin in Jiang, Zhe, Jinghu, Fujian, and Guangnan Circuits; he reached Wanzhou and died of illness on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Vice Director of the Bureau of Garrison Affairs, he was appointed commissioner for mining, smelting, and iron coin across the Jiang, Zhe, Jinghu, Fujian, and Guangnan circuits. He reached Wanzhou and died of illness on the road.

sentences.zh: 黃震，字伯起，建州浦城人。

translations.literal: Huang Zhen, styled Boqi, a native of Pucheng in Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhen, styled Boqi, was a native of Pucheng in Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，累遷著作佐郎、通判遂州。

translations.literal: Passed the jinshi examination, incrementally promoted to Assistant Archivist and supervising prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and rose through the ranks to Assistant Archivist and supervising prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗給兩川軍士緡錢，詔至西川，而東川獨不及，軍士謀為變。

translations.literal: Once when string-cash was issued to the Two Chuan garrison troops, the edict reached West Chuan but East Chuan alone was not included; the soldiers plotted mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when string-cash was issued to garrison troops in the Two Chuan region, the edict reached West Chuan but not East Chuan. The soldiers there plotted mutiny.

sentences.zh: 震白主者曰：「朝廷豈忘東川邪？

translations.literal: Zhen informed the chief official: "Would the court forget East Chuan?
translations.idiomatic: Zhen told the responsible official, "Surely the court has not forgotten East Chuan?

sentences.zh: 殆詔書稽留爾。」

translations.literal: Probably the edict is merely delayed."
translations.idiomatic: The edict has probably just been delayed."

sentences.zh: 即開州帑給錢如西川，眾乃定，明日詔至。

translations.literal: He immediately opened the prefectural treasury and issued cash as in West Chuan; the crowd then settled; the next day the edict arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately opened the prefectural treasury and distributed cash on the same terms as West Chuan. The troops settled down, and the edict arrived the next day.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書都官員外郎、提點湖北路刑獄，還，判三司磨勘司，擢江淮發運使。

translations.literal: Incrementally promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Retainers in the Secretariat, commissioner for penal affairs in Hubei Circuit; returned, served in the Three Departments Audit Bureau, promoted to Huai-Jiang grain transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Bureau of Retainers and commissioner for penal affairs in Hubei Circuit, returned to court to serve in the Three Departments Audit Bureau, and was promoted to Huai-Jiang grain transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先是，李溥自三司小吏為發運使十餘年，奸贓狼籍，丁謂黨之，無敢言者。

translations.literal: Previously, Li Pu rose from a minor clerk in the Three Departments to grain transport commissioner for more than ten years; his corruption and embezzlement were notorious; Ding Wei protected him, and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Li Pu had risen from a minor clerk in the Three Departments to grain transport commissioner and held the post for more than ten years. His corruption was notorious, Ding Wei shielded him, and no one dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 震將行，上書自陳，辭頗憤激，真宗知其意在溥也，諭之曰：「卿當與人和。」

translations.literal: When Zhen was about to depart, he submitted a memorial stating his case; the language was rather indignant. Emperor Zhenzong knew his intent was aimed at Pu and instructed him: "You should harmonize with others."
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhen departed, he submitted a memorial stating his case in language that was rather heated. Emperor Zhenzong knew his target was Li Pu and admonished him: "You should keep the peace with others."

sentences.zh: 震對曰：「廉正公忠，臣職也。

translations.literal: Zhen replied: "Integrity, uprightness, public loyalty—these are a minister's duties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied, "Integrity, uprightness, and public loyalty are a minister's duties.

sentences.zh: 負陛下任使者，臣不敢與之和。」

translations.literal: One whom Your Majesty entrusts with office—I dare not harmonize with him."
translations.idiomatic: As one entrusted by Your Majesty with this mission, I dare not make peace with corruption."

sentences.zh: 既至，發溥奸贓數十事，溥坐廢；

translations.literal: Upon arrival, he exposed dozens of Pu's corrupt acts; Pu was removed from office;
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, he exposed dozens of Pu's corrupt acts, and Pu was dismissed from office;

sentences.zh: 而震亦為溥訟，奪一官。

translations.literal: but Zhen also was sued by Pu and stripped of one rank.
translations.idiomatic: but Pu also brought suit against Zhen, who was stripped of one rank.

sentences.zh: 罷，畏謂權，不敢自直，及謂貶，乃復官，知饒州，徙廣東轉運使。

translations.literal: After dismissal, he feared Ding Wei's power and dared not clear himself; once Wei was demoted, he was restored to office, made prefect of Raozhou, transferred as transport commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After his dismissal he feared Ding Wei's power and dared not clear his name. Once Wei was demoted, Zhen was restored to office, appointed prefect of Raozhou, and then transferred to transport commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 廣南歲進異花數千本，至都下枯死者十八九，道路苦其煩擾，震奏罷之。

translations.literal: Guangnan annually presented several thousand exotic flowers; when they reached the capital eight or nine in ten withered and died; the roads suffered from the nuisance; Zhen memorialized to abolish this.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnan annually sent several thousand exotic flowers as tribute; eight or nine in ten withered and died by the time they reached the capital, and the roads groaned under the burden. Zhen memorialized to abolish the practice.

sentences.zh: 震在真宗朝數論事，既卒，詔進其官一等。

translations.literal: Zhen often discussed affairs under Zhenzong; after his death, an edict advanced his rank one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had often remonstrated on policy under Emperor Zhenzong. After his death, an edict advanced his rank by one grade.

sentences.zh: 胡順之

translations.literal: Hu Shunzhi
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shunzhi

sentences.zh: 胡順之，字孝先，原州臨涇人。

translations.literal: Hu Shunzhi, styled Xiaoxian, a native of Linjing in Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shunzhi, styled Xiaoxian, was a native of Linjing in Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，試秘書省校書郎、知休寧縣。

translations.literal: Passed the jinshi examination, appointed proofreader in the Secretariat, prefect of Xiuning County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed proofreader in the Secretariat, and served as prefect of Xiuning County.

sentences.zh: 民有汪姓者豪橫，縣不能制，歲租賦常不入，適以訟逮捕，不肯出。

translations.literal: Among the people was one surnamed Wang who was overbearing; the county could not control him; yearly rent and tax payments often did not come in; when he was summoned to court on a lawsuit and arrested, he refused to come out.
translations.idiomatic: A man surnamed Wang among the people was domineering and lawless. The county could not control him, and he routinely failed to pay rent and taxes. When he was summoned to court on a lawsuit and officers came to arrest him, he refused to come out.

sentences.zh: 順之曰：「令不行何以為政。」

translations.literal: Shunzhi said: "If orders are not enforced, how can one govern?"
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi said, "If the law cannot be enforced, how can one govern?"

sentences.zh: 命積薪環而焚之，豪大駭，少長趨出，叩頭伏辜，推其長械送州，致之法。

translations.literal: He ordered firewood piled around and set alight; the magnate was terrified; young and old rushed out, kowtowed and submitted to punishment; he had the clan head shackled and sent to the prefecture, brought to justice.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered firewood piled around the compound and set alight. The magnate was terrified; young and old rushed out, kowtowed, and submitted to punishment. Shunzhi had the clan head shackled and sent to the prefecture to face the law.

sentences.zh: 為青州從事。

translations.literal: He served as aide in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as an aide in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 高麗入貢，中貴人挾以為重，使州官旅拜於郊。

translations.literal: When Goryeo came to pay tribute, a palace eunuch leveraged this for importance and made prefectural officials bow in formation in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: When Goryeo came to pay tribute, a palace eunuch used the occasion to assert his importance and made prefectural officials bow in formation outside the city.

sentences.zh: 順之曰：「青，大鎮也。

translations.literal: Shunzhi said: "Qing is a great garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi said, "Qing is a major garrison command.

sentences.zh: 在唐押新羅、渤海，奈何卑屈如此？」

translations.literal: In Tang it kept Silla and Bohai in check—how can we demean ourselves like this?"
translations.idiomatic: In Tang times it kept Silla and Bohai in check. How can we demean ourselves like this?"

sentences.zh: 獨不拜。

translations.literal: He alone did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: He alone refused to bow.

sentences.zh: 大姓麻士瑤陰結貴侍，匿兵械，服用擬尚方，親黨僕使甚多，州縣被陵蔑，莫敢發其姦。

translations.literal: The powerful clan member Ma Shi Yao secretly allied with noble attendants, concealed weapons, used dress and implements approximating the Imperial Workshop; relatives, clients, and servants were numerous; prefectures and counties were insulted and none dared expose his wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shi Yao, a man of a powerful clan, secretly allied with palace favorites, hoarded weapons, and used dress and furnishings fit for the imperial workshops. His kin, clients, and servants were legion, and prefectures and counties suffered his contempt, yet none dared expose his crimes.

sentences.zh: 會士瑤殺兄子溫裕，其母訴於州，眾相視曰：「孰敢往捕者？」

translations.literal: When Shi Yao killed his elder brother's son Wen Yu, the mother appealed to the prefecture; everyone looked at one another: "Who would dare go to arrest him?"
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Yao killed his elder brother's son Wen Yu, the boy's mother appealed to the prefecture. Everyone looked at one another and asked, "Who would dare go and arrest him?"

sentences.zh: 順之持檄徑去，盡得其黨。

translations.literal: Shunzhi took his warrant and went straight there, capturing all his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi took his warrant and went straight to the scene, capturing the entire faction.

sentences.zh: 有詔鞫問，士瑤論死，其子弟坐流放者百餘人。

translations.literal: An edict ordered interrogation; Shi Yao was sentenced to death; over a hundred of his sons and younger kinsmen were exiled.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a full inquiry. Shi Yao was sentenced to death, and more than a hundred of his sons and younger kinsmen were exiled.

sentences.zh: 改著作佐郎、知常熟縣，遷秘書丞，分司南京。

translations.literal: Changed to Assistant Archivist, prefect of Changshu County, promoted to Secretary Director, serving at the Southern Capital as a detached official.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Assistant Archivist and prefect of Changshu County, promoted to Secretary Director, and assigned to serve at the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: When Renzong acceded, he was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong acceded, he was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 天聖、明道間，再上宰相書，乞太后還政，宰相匿不以聞。

translations.literal: Between Tiansheng and Mingdao he twice submitted letters to the chief counselor, begging the Empress Dowager to return power; the chief counselor concealed them and did not report.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng and Mingdao eras he twice wrote to the chief counselor begging the Empress Dowager to restore the emperor's authority. The chief counselor suppressed the letters and never reported them.

sentences.zh: 太后崩，順之附疾置自言，求其書，出宰相家。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager died, Shunzhi, feigning illness at his station, spoke up and demanded his letters—they emerged from the chief counselor's house.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager died, Shunzhi, feigning illness at his post, spoke up and demanded his letters back. They were produced from the chief counselor's house.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘉其忠，特遷尚書屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: Renzong praised his loyalty and specially promoted him to Vice Director of the Bureau of Public Lands in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong praised his loyalty and specially promoted him to Vice Director of the Bureau of Public Lands.

sentences.zh: 其後數論朝廷事，仲淹愛其才，然挾術尚權，喜縱橫捭闔。

translations.literal: Thereafter he often discussed court affairs; Fan Zhongyan admired his talent, yet he relied on stratagems, valued power, and delighted in maneuver and persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he often spoke on court affairs. Fan Zhongyan admired his talent, but he relied on stratagem, valued power, and delighted in political maneuver.

sentences.zh: 以目失明廢，州里皆憚焉。

translations.literal: He was dismissed because of blindness in one eye; people throughout the prefecture feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed after losing sight in one eye, yet people throughout the prefecture still feared him.

sentences.zh: 陳貫，字仲通，其先相州安陽人，後葬其父河陽，因家焉。

translations.literal: Chen Guan, styled Zhongtong; his ancestors were from Anyang in Xiangzhou; later he buried his father at Heyang and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guan, styled Zhongtong, came from a family originally of Anyang in Xiangzhou. After burying his father at Heyang, he settled there.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻，數上疏言邊事。

translations.literal: In youth he was free-spirited and repeatedly submitted memorials on frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was bold and unconventional, and he repeatedly submitted memorials on frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，真宗識貫名，擢置高第。

translations.literal: Passed the jinshi examination; Zhenzong recognized Guan's name and placed him in the top tier.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination. Emperor Zhenzong recognized his name and placed him in the highest tier.

sentences.zh: 為臨安縣主簿，以秘書省著作佐郎為刑部詳覆官，改秘書丞，為審刑院詳議官，歷知衛州、涇州。

translations.literal: Registrar of Lin'an County; as Assistant Archivist in the Secretariat served as reviewing officer of the Ministry of Justice; changed to Secretary Director; reviewing officer of the Court for the Review of Punishments; successively prefect of Weizhou and Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as registrar of Lin'an County, then as Assistant Archivist and reviewing officer of the Ministry of Justice, later as Secretary Director and reviewing officer of the Court for the Review of Punishments, and successively as prefect of Weizhou and Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 督察盜賊，禁戢不肖子弟，簿書筦庫，賦租出入，皆自檢核。

translations.literal: He inspected bandits and robbers, restrained unworthy sons and younger brothers, and personally checked accounts, stores, and the inflow and outflow of tax rents.
translations.idiomatic: He cracked down on bandits and robbers, restrained unruly sons of good families, and personally audited the ledgers, stores, and all inflow and outflow of tax revenue.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂僚屬曰：「視縣官物如己物，容有姦乎？」

translations.literal: He once told his staff: "If one regarded the county's goods as one's own goods, could there be corruption?"
translations.idiomatic: He once told his staff, "If one treated the county's property as one's own, could there be corruption?"

sentences.zh: 州人憚其嚴。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture feared his severity.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the prefecture feared his strictness.

sentences.zh: 擢利州路轉運使。

translations.literal: Promoted to transport commissioner of Lizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to transport commissioner of Lizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，出職田粟賑饑者，又帥富民令計口占粟，悉發其餘。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he released grain from official fields to relieve the hungry; he also led the wealthy to reckon grain by head count and release all surplus.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine he released grain from official fields to feed the hungry, and also ordered wealthy households to reckon grain by head count and surrender all surplus stores.

sentences.zh: 徙陝西，累遷尚書度支員外郎，入為三司鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: Transferred to Shaanxi, incrementally promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Revenue in the Secretariat, entered service as judicial intendant of the Salt and Iron Bureau of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Shaanxi, rose to Vice Director of the Bureau of Revenue, and entered court service as judicial intendant of the Three Departments' Salt and Iron Bureau.

sentences.zh: 領河北轉運使，請疏徐、鮑、曹、易四水，興屯田。

translations.literal: Headed Hebei transport commissioner, petitioned to dredge the Xu, Bao, Cao, and Yi rivers and develop military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: As head of Hebei transport commissioner, he petitioned to dredge the Xu, Bao, Cao, and Yi rivers and establish military colonies.

sentences.zh: 徙河東，歷三司戶部、鹽鐵副使，以刑部郎中直昭文館，知相州。

translations.literal: Transferred to Hedong, served as Vice Commissioner of the Household and Salt and Iron Bureaus of the Three Departments, as Director of the Ministry of Justice concurrently at the Hall for Spreading Culture, prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hedong, served as Vice Commissioner of the Three Departments' Household and Salt and Iron Bureaus, held concurrent posts as Director of the Ministry of Justice and at the Hall for Spreading Culture, and was prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 還朝卒。

translations.literal: Returned to court and died.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court and died there.

sentences.zh: 貫喜言兵，咸平中，大將楊瓊、王榮喪師而歸，貫上書曰：:「前日不斬傅潛、張昭允，使瓊輩畏死不畏法，請自今合戰而奔者，主校皆斬；

translations.literal: Guan delighted in discussing military matters; in the Xianping era, the great generals Yang Qiong and Wang Rong returned after losing their armies; Guan submitted a memorial saying: "Previously failing to execute Fu Qian and Zhang Zhaoyun made men like Qiong fear death but not the law. I request that from now on, in combined battle, all who flee—the commanding officers be executed;
translations.idiomatic: Guan loved to discuss military affairs. In the Xianping era, after the great generals Yang Qiong and Wang Rong returned having lost their armies, Guan submitted a memorial: "Because Fu Qian and Zhang Zhaoyun were not executed earlier, men like Qiong fear death but not the law. I request that henceforth, in a general engagement, any commander who flees be executed;

sentences.zh: 大將戰死，裨校無傷而還，與奔軍同。

translations.literal: if a great general dies in battle but deputy commanders return unharmed, they are the same as fleeing troops.
translations.idiomatic: if a commanding general dies in battle but his deputy commanders return unharmed, they should be treated the same as deserters.

sentences.zh: 軍衄城圍，別部力足救而不至者，以逗留論。」

translations.literal: When the army is defeated and a city besieged, if another unit has strength enough to rescue but does not arrive, it should be judged as delay."
translations.idiomatic: When an army is routed and a city besieged, any separate unit with strength enough to rescue but failing to arrive should be prosecuted for delay."

sentences.zh: 真宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: Zhenzong praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong praised and adopted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 又嘗上《形勢》、《選將》、《練兵論》三篇，大略言地有六害：

translations.literal: He also once submitted three treatises—On Strategic Situation, On Selecting Generals, and On Training Troops—summarily stating that terrain has six harms:
translations.idiomatic: He also once submitted three treatises—On Strategic Situation, On Selecting Generals, and On Training Troops—in which he broadly argued that terrain has six hazards:

sentences.zh: 「今北邊既失古北之險，然自威虜城東距海三百里，沮澤磽確，所謂天設地造，非敵所能輕入。

translations.literal: "Today the northern frontier has already lost the defense of Gubei Pass; yet from Weilü City eastward to the sea stretches three hundred li of marsh, bog, and barren hard ground—what may be called heaven-made and earth-formed; the enemy cannot lightly enter.
translations.idiomatic: "The northern frontier has already lost the defense of Gubei Pass, yet from Weilü City eastward to the sea stretches three hundred li of marsh, bog, and barren hard ground—terrain heaven and earth themselves have shaped, which the enemy cannot lightly penetrate.

sentences.zh: 由威虜西極狼山不百里，地廣平，利馳突，此必爭之地。

translations.literal: From Weilü westward to Langshan is less than one hundred li; the land is broad and flat, favorable for cavalry charges—this is ground that must be contested.
translations.idiomatic: West of Weilü to Langshan is less than a hundred li of broad, flat ground ideal for cavalry charges—terrain that both sides must fight to hold.

sentences.zh: 凡爭地之利，先居則佚，後起則勞，宜有以待之。

translations.literal: In general, for the advantage of contested ground, whoever occupies it first rests at ease, while whoever arrives later labors—we should have preparations awaiting this.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever holds contested ground first rests easy while the latecomer toils; we should be ready and waiting for that fight.

sentences.zh: 昔李漢超守瀛州，契丹不敢視關南尺寸地。

translations.literal: Formerly when Li Hanchao defended Yingzhou, the Khitan did not dare cast an eye on a single inch of Guannan land.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hanchao once held Yingzhou, the Khitan did not dare covet even an inch of territory south of the passes.

sentences.zh: 今將帥大抵用恩澤進，雖謹重可信，卒與敵遇，方略何從而出邪？

translations.literal: Today commanders are for the most part promoted through imperial favor; though prudent and trustworthy, when they suddenly meet the enemy, from what source can strategy emerge?
translations.idiomatic: Today's commanders rise mostly through imperial favor. They may be prudent and trustworthy, but when they suddenly face the enemy, where will strategy come from?

sentences.zh: 故敵勢益張，兵折於外者二十年。

translations.literal: Therefore the enemy's power grew ever greater, and armies broken abroad—for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the enemy's power has steadily grown and our armies have been broken on the frontier for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 方國家收天下材勇以備禁旅，賴廩給賜予而已，恬於休息，久不識戰，可以衛京師，不可以戍邊境。

translations.literal: Just now the state gathers talent and the brave from across the realm to supply the Imperial Guard, relying only on granary rations and bestowals, content in rest, long unfamiliar with battle—they can guard the capital but cannot garrison the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The state now gathers the brave from across the realm for the Imperial Guard, fed on rations and stipends, long at ease and unused to war. They can defend the capital but cannot hold the frontier.

sentences.zh: 請募土人隸本軍，籍丁民為府兵，使北捍契丹，西捍夏人。

translations.literal: I request recruiting locals attached to the home army, registering adult males as district militia, to defend north against the Khitan and west against the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: I propose recruiting local men into frontier regiments and registering adult males as district militia to hold the north against the Khitan and the west against the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 敵之情偽，地勢之險易，彼皆素知，可不戰而屈人之兵矣。」

translations.literal: The enemy's true and false dispositions, the terrain's difficulty and ease—they all know these by nature; one can subdue the enemy's army without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: They already know the enemy's every feint and the lay of the land; they could break the enemy's will without a battle."

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 著《兵略》，世頗稱之。

translations.literal: He authored Military Strategy, and the age fairly praised it.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Military Strategy, which his contemporaries widely praised.

sentences.zh: 子安石。

translations.literal: His son was An Shi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was An Shi.

sentences.zh: 子 安石

translations.literal: Son: An Shi
translations.idiomatic: Son: An Shi

sentences.zh: 安石，字子堅，以蔭鎖廳及第。

translations.literal: An Shi, style Zijian, passed the examination through yin privilege at the Suo Hall.
translations.idiomatic: An Shi, styled Zijian, passed the palace examination by inherited privilege through the Suo Hall.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，為夔、峽轉運判官。

translations.literal: In the Jiayou era, he served as transport intendant of Kuizhou and Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiayou era he served as transport intendant for Kuizhou and Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 民蓄蠱毒殺人，捕誅其魁並得良藥圖，由是遇毒者得不死。

translations.literal: The people kept poison-gu to kill men; he captured and executed the ringleaders and also obtained diagrams of effective remedies; from this, those who encountered poison did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Locals kept venomous gu creatures to kill people. He captured and executed the ringleaders and obtained charts of effective antidotes, so that thereafter victims of poisoning could be saved.

sentences.zh: 提點陝西刑獄，攝帥鄜延，能用諜者，敵動靜輒先聞。

translations.literal: As judicial intendant of Shaanxi punishments, he acted as commanding general of Fuyan, able to employ spies; the enemy's movements he always heard of first.
translations.idiomatic: As Shaanxi judicial intendant he also served as acting commander of Fuyan. Skilled at employing spies, he invariably learned of enemy movements before they occurred.

sentences.zh: 嘗敕邊民戒嚴，既而數萬騎奄至，無所獲而去，璽書嘉之。

translations.literal: Once he ordered frontier people to stand on alert; soon after, tens of thousands of horsemen arrived suddenly, gained nothing, and departed; an imperial edict in the emperor's own hand praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he ordered the frontier population to stand on alert; soon tens of thousands of enemy horsemen descended without warning, found nothing to plunder, and withdrew. The emperor rewarded him with a personal edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 歷使京西、河東、淮南、京東，知蘇州、邠州、河中府。

translations.literal: He successively served as commissioner for Jingxi, Hedong, Huainan, and Jingdong, and was prefect of Suzhou, Binzhou, and the Hezhong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as commissioner for Jingxi, Hedong, Huainan, and Jingdong, and was prefect of Suzhou and Binzhou and governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 戶部副使韓絳鎮太原，議行鹽法，與監司多不合，加安石集賢殿修撰，為河東都轉運使，議始定。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner of the Household Bureau Han Jiang garrisoned Taiyuan and debated implementing the salt law; he disagreed with many supervisors and commissioners; An Shi was added as compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and made chief transport commissioner of Hedong, and only then was the plan settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jiang, Vice Commissioner of the Household Bureau, was stationed at Taiyuan and debated implementing the salt law, he clashed with many supervisory officials. An Shi was appointed compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and chief transport commissioner of Hedong, and only then was the policy settled.

sentences.zh: 謂其僚曰：「興事當有漸，急則擾。」

translations.literal: He told his staff: "When undertaking a project there should be gradual progress; if rushed, it causes disturbance."
translations.idiomatic: He told his staff, "New policies should be rolled out gradually; haste only provokes unrest."

sentences.zh: 乃出鹽付民而俾之券，使隨所得貿易，鬻畢而歸券，私販為減。

translations.literal: He then issued salt to the people and gave them certificates, allowing them to trade according to what they obtained; when sale was finished they returned the certificates, and private trafficking was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He issued salt to the people with certificates allowing them to trade freely, requiring the certificates to be returned once the salt was sold. Private trafficking declined as a result.

sentences.zh: 進天章閣待制。

translations.literal: Promoted to Hanlin Archivist of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin Archivist of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations.

sentences.zh: 官軍西征時，遣縣令佐督餉，安石謂文吏畏怯，武人邀功，乃但取敢行者。

translations.literal: When the official army marched west on campaign, county magistrates and assistants were sent to supervise supplies; An Shi said civil officials were timid and military men sought glory, so he took only those bold enough to act.
translations.idiomatic: During the western campaign, county magistrates and assistants were dispatched to supervise supplies. An Shi argued that civil officials were too timid and military men too eager for glory, and chose only men bold enough to get the job done.

sentences.zh: 申約束以防眾潰，曰：「事不豫警，俟其犯而誅之，是罔民也。」

translations.literal: He proclaimed regulations to prevent mass rout, saying: "If affairs are not warned of in advance, waiting until they violate and then executing them—is to deceive the people."
translations.idiomatic: He issued strict regulations to prevent mass desertion, saying, "If you do not warn people in advance and only punish them after they offend, you are deceiving the people."

sentences.zh: 王中正帥東師而西，報安石持四十日糧，而師駐白草平彌月。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongzheng led eastern troops westward and reported to An Shi that he held forty days' grain, yet the army camped at Baicao Ping for a full month.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongzheng led eastern troops westward and told An Shi he had forty days' rations, yet the army remained encamped at Baicao Ping for a full month.

sentences.zh: 安石深念曰：「吾頓兵益久，而秦甲未至，倘不足於食，將以乏軍興罪我。」

translations.literal: An Shi thought deeply and said: "I have kept the army halted ever longer, yet Qin armor has not arrived; if food should prove insufficient, I will be charged with failing the army's provisioning."
translations.idiomatic: An Shi worried aloud, "The longer this army sits idle, the longer we wait for supplies from Qin. If rations run short, I will be blamed for starving the campaign."

sentences.zh: 即擅發民再餉，乃以聞。

translations.literal: He immediately on his own authority mobilized the people to deliver supplies a second time, then reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Without authorization he mobilized the people to deliver a second round of supplies, then reported what he had done.

sentences.zh: 李舜舉劾其專，詔置獄於潞，安石自麟州會逮，俄而他路饋糧多不繼，神宗察其無罪，赦之。

translations.literal: Li Shunju impeached him for arbitrariness; an edict set up a prison at Lu; An Shi from Linzhou came to submit to arrest; soon grain from other routes mostly failed to keep up; Shenzong perceived he was without guilt and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shunju impeached him for acting on his own authority. An edict ordered a prison established at Lu, and An Shi surrendered himself from Linzhou. Soon supplies from other routes mostly failed to keep pace. Emperor Shenzong judged him innocent and pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 尚書省初建，召為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Department of State Affairs was first established, he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Household Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When the Department of State Affairs was first established, he was summoned to serve as Vice Minister of the Household Bureau.

sentences.zh: 嘗與右曹李定同奏事，帝目留之曰：「卿豈非在淮南日不肯保李定持服者乎？」

translations.literal: Once, when he joined Li Ding of the Right Section in presenting business to the throne, the emperor kept his gaze on him and said, "Are you not the one who during your days in Huainan refused to vouch for Li Ding's observance of mourning?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, when he joined Li Ding of the Right Section in presenting business to the throne, the emperor fixed his gaze on him and said, "Are you not the one who during your days in Huainan refused to vouch for Li Ding's observance of mourning?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「詔問臣，臣不敢不以實奏。」

translations.literal: He replied, "The edict questioned me; I dared not report other than the facts."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The edict questioned me, and I dared not report other than the facts."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「以實事君，朕所與也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Serving the ruler with facts is what I value."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Serving the ruler with facts is what I value."

sentences.zh: 進吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 選人將改京官，須次久，臨當引對，率困於刑寺審問，或沮以微文，則一跌不復。

translations.literal: Candidates for transfer to capital office had long waits in the queue; when the moment came for their presentation audience, they were routinely worn down by interrogation at the Criminal Bureau, or thwarted by trivial violations of form—and one fall meant no recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates awaiting transfer to capital office posts waited long in the queue; when the moment came for their presentation audience, they were routinely worn down by interrogation at the Criminal Bureau or thwarted by trivial violations of form—and one misstep meant no recovery.

sentences.zh: 安石則罷再問，以絕曩弊，遂為後法。

translations.literal: An Shi abolished the second interrogation to end long-standing abuses, and this became the practice thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: An Shi abolished the second interrogation to end long-standing abuses, and this became the precedent thereafter.

sentences.zh: 出知永興軍、鄧、襄、陳、鄭州、河陽，至龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: He left the capital to serve as military commissioner of Yongxing and prefect of Deng, Xiang, Chen, and Zheng prefectures and Hezhong, rising to academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital to serve as military commissioner of Yongxing and prefect of Deng, Xiang, Chen, and Zheng prefectures and Hezhong, rising to academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In Shaosheng 1 he died, at age eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shaosheng 1, at age eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 范祥，字晉公，邠州三水人。

translations.literal: Fan Xiang, style Jingong, a native of Sanshui in Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xiang, styled Jingong, was a native of Sanshui in Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，自乾州推官稍遷殿中丞、通判鎮戎軍。

translations.literal: Passed the jinshi examination, from magistrate of Qianzhou gradually promoted to Director in the Court of Imperial Ceremonial and military supervisor of Zhenrong Army.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi graduate, he rose from magistrate of Qianzhou to Director in the Court of Imperial Ceremonial and military supervisor of Zhenrong Army.

sentences.zh: 元昊圍城急，祥帥將士拒退之。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed the siege urgently, Xiang led officers and soldiers to repel and drive him back.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao pressed the siege hard, Fan Xiang led his troops in repelling him.

sentences.zh: 請築劉璠堡、定川砦，從之。

translations.literal: He requested building Liu Fan Fort and Dingchuan Stockade; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to build Liu Fan Fort and Dingchuan Stockade, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 歷知慶、汝、華三州，提舉陝西銀銅坑冶鑄錢。

translations.literal: He successively governed Qing, Ru, and Hua prefectures, and supervised Shaanxi silver, copper, mining, smelting, and coin casting.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Qing, Ru, and Hua, and supervised Shaanxi's silver and copper mines, smelters, and mints.

sentences.zh: 祥曉達財利，建議變鹽法，後人不敢易，稍加損益，人輒不便，語在《食貨志》。

translations.literal: Xiang was thoroughly versed in revenue and profit; he proposed changing the salt law; later men did not dare alter it; when slightly added to or reduced, people at once found it inconvenient—the account is in the Treatise on Food and Money.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xiang understood fiscal affairs well. He proposed reforming the salt law, and his successors dared not change it. Even minor adjustments provoked public discontent—the details appear in the Treatise on Food and Money.

sentences.zh: 提點本路刑獄，制置解鹽，累遷度支員外郎，權轉運副使。

translations.literal: Judicial intendant of this circuit's punishments, director of Jie Salt, incrementally promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Revenue, acting Vice Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As judicial intendant of the circuit, he supervised Jie Salt production, rose to Vice Director of the Bureau of Revenue, and served as acting Vice Transport Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 古渭砦距秦州三百里，道經啞兒峽，邊城數請城之，朝廷以饋餉之艱不許。

translations.literal: Guwei Stockade was three hundred li from Qinzhou; the route passed through Ya'er Gorge; frontier posts repeatedly requested fortifying it; the court did not permit it because of the hardship of supplying provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Guwei Stockade lay three hundred li from Qinzhou along a route through Ya'er Gorge. Frontier commanders repeatedly petitioned to fortify it, but the court refused because resupply would be too difficult.

sentences.zh: 祥權領州事，驟請修築，未報，輒自興役。

translations.literal: Xiang acting in charge of prefectural affairs urgently requested repair and construction; before reply came, he on his own launched the labor.
translations.idiomatic: While acting prefect, Fan Xiang urgently petitioned to build the fort. Before any reply arrived, he began construction on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 蕃部驚擾，青唐族羌攻破廣吳嶺堡，圍啞兒峽砦，官軍戰死者千餘人，坐削一官，知唐州。

translations.literal: Tribal peoples were alarmed and disturbed; the Qingtang clans and Qiang broke Guangwu Ridge Fort, besieged Ya'er Gorge Stockade; over a thousand government troops died in battle; punished by demotion of one rank, he was made prefect of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal peoples were thrown into turmoil. Qingtang Qiang raiders stormed Guangwu Ridge Fort and besieged Ya'er Gorge Stockade. More than a thousand government troops died in the fighting. Fan Xiang was demoted one rank and appointed prefect of Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 後復官，提舉陝西緣邊青、白鹽，改制置解鹽使，卒。

translations.literal: Later his rank was restored; he supervised Shaanxi frontier green and white salt; was made Director of Jie Salt; died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored to rank, supervised green and white salt along the Shaanxi frontier, was appointed Director of Jie Salt, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，包拯言：「祥通陝西鹽法，行之十年，歲減榷貨務使緡錢數百萬，其勞可錄。」

translations.literal: In the Jiayou era, Bao Zheng said: "Xiang implemented the Shaanxi salt law; practiced for ten years, annually reducing the Monopoly Goods Bureau's string-cash by several million; his service merits recording."
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiayou era, Bao Zheng said, "Fan Xiang implemented the Shaanxi salt law. Over ten years it saved the Monopoly Goods Bureau several million strings of cash annually. His service deserves recognition."

sentences.zh: 官其子孫景郊社齋郎。

translations.literal: His son Sun Jing was appointed Ceremonial Attendant of the Suburban Altar.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Jing was appointed Ceremonial Attendant of the Suburban Altar.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，平洮、岷、疊、宕、河州數千里，置郡縣，以古渭為通遠軍。

translations.literal: In the Xining era, pacifying Tao, Min, Die, Dang, and He prefectures over several thousand li, establishing commanderies and counties, making Guwei into Tongyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era the court pacified Tao, Min, Die, Dang, and He over thousands of li, established administrative districts, and made Guwei into Tongyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 權陝西轉運副使張詵奏：「朝廷復洮、隴故地，自將帥至裨佐悉有功賞。

translations.literal: Acting Shaanxi Vice Transport Commissioner Zhang Shen memorialized: "The court has recovered the old lands of Tao and Long; from commanding generals down to deputy officers all received merit rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Shaanxi Vice Transport Commissioner Zhang Shen memorialized, "When the court recovered the old Tao and Long territories, every commander down to junior officer received merit rewards.

sentences.zh: 臣見洮、渭父老言，皇祐中，轉運使祥因熟羌數被寇掠，其部族願輸土置城以為守禦，乃即古渭為砦。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard old men of Tao and Wei say: in the Huangyou era, Transport Commissioner Xiang, because the settled Qiang had repeatedly been raided and plundered, and their clans wished to surrender land to establish a fort for defense, thereupon made Guwei into a stockade.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard elders in Tao and Wei say that during the Huangyou era, Transport Commissioner Fan Xiang, learning that settled Qiang tribes had been repeatedly raided and wished to surrender land for a defensive fort, established a stockade at Guwei.

sentences.zh: 祥此舉足以消沮邊隙，可謂知攻守之利矣。

translations.literal: Xiang's act was sufficient to dampen frontier friction; it may be called knowing the advantage of attack and defense.
translations.idiomatic: This act alone helped check frontier conflict. Fan Xiang truly understood the principles of attack and defense.

sentences.zh: 兵出少挫，身黜謀廢，臣竊悲之。

translations.literal: When troops went out and suffered a slight setback, he was personally demoted and his plan abandoned; your subject privately grieves this.
translations.idiomatic: After one minor defeat his career was ruined and his plan discarded. I find that deeply regrettable.

sentences.zh: 冀推原舊功，少賜褒恤，使天下知祥死猶被恩，且舒祥忠義之氣。」

translations.literal: I hope to trace back to his former merit, grant a little praise and consolation, so that all under Heaven know Xiang after death still received grace, and moreover ease Xiang's spirit of loyalty and righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that his original merit be recognized with some posthumous honor, so that all may know Fan Xiang was rewarded even in death, and so that his loyal spirit may rest in peace."

sentences.zh: 詔贈秘書，錄一子未官者。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Secretary and enrolled one son who had not yet held office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Fan Xiang posthumously appointed Secretary and enrolled one of his sons who had not yet held office.

sentences.zh: 子育。

translations.literal: His son was Yu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yu.

sentences.zh: 子 育

translations.literal: Son: Yu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yu

sentences.zh: 育，字巽之，舉進士，為涇陽令。

translations.literal: Yu, style Xunzhi, passed the jinshi examination, and was magistrate of Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, styled Xunzhi, passed the jinshi examination and served as magistrate of Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 以養親謁歸，從張載學。

translations.literal: To care for his parents he requested leave and returned home, studying under Zhang Zai.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home on leave to care for his parents and studied under Zhang Zai.

sentences.zh: 有薦之者，召見，授崇文校書、監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: Someone recommended him; he was summoned for audience and granted Compiler at the Hall of Promoting Literature and Acting Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When someone recommended him, he was summoned to court and appointed Compiler at the Hall of Promoting Literature and Acting Censor.

sentences.zh: 神宗喻之曰：「《書》稱『聖讒說殄行』，此朕任御史之意也。」

translations.literal: Shenzong instructed him: "The Documents says 'The sage exterminates evil words and perverse conduct'—this is my intent in appointing you censor."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong told him, "The Documents says, 'The sage cuts off slander and ends wicked conduct.' That is why I have made you a censor."

sentences.zh: 育請用《大學》誠意、正心以治天下國家，因薦載等數人。

translations.literal: Yu requested using the Great Learning's sincerity of purpose and rectification of mind to govern all under Heaven and the state, and thereupon recommended Zhang Zai and several others.
translations.idiomatic: Yu urged governing the realm through the Great Learning's ideals of sincere purpose and rectified mind, and recommended Zhang Zai and several others.

sentences.zh: 西夏入環慶，詔育行邊，還言：「寶元、康定間，王師與夏人三大戰而三北，今再舉亦然。

translations.literal: When the Western Xia entered Huan and Qing, an edict ordered Yu to inspect the frontier; returning he said: "Between Baoyuan and Kangding, the imperial army fought the Tangut in three great battles and was defeated thrice; now raised again it is the same.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut invaded Huan and Qing, Yu was ordered to inspect the frontier. On his return he said, "During the Baoyuan and Kangding era the imperial army fought three major battles against the Tangut and lost all three. The same pattern holds today.

sentences.zh: 豈中國之大，不足以支夏人數郡乎？

translations.literal: Can China's vastness not suffice to sustain against the Tangut's several commanderies?
translations.idiomatic: Is the Middle Kingdom so vast that it cannot stand against a few Tangut prefectures?

sentences.zh: 由不察彼己，妄舉而驟用之爾。

translations.literal: It is from not examining them and us, rashly undertaking and suddenly employing troops—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The problem is that we do not weigh their strength against ours, but rashly launch campaigns and throw untested forces into battle.

sentences.zh: 昨荔原之役，夏人聲言：『我自修壘，不與漢爭。』

translations.literal: In yesterday's Liyuan campaign, the Tangut proclaimed: 'We ourselves are repairing fortifications and do not contend with the Han.'
translations.idiomatic: In the recent battle at Liyuan the Tangut declared, 'We are only repairing our fortifications and do not seek conflict with the Han.'

sentences.zh: 三犯之，然後掩殺，雖追奔亦不至境。

translations.literal: Three times we violated this, and only then did they ambush and kill; even in pursuit they did not reach the border.
translations.idiomatic: We violated their positions three times before they struck in ambush. Even when pursued they would not cross the border.

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，其情大可見矣。」

translations.literal: Observing from this, their disposition can be clearly seen."
translations.idiomatic: From this their true intentions are plain."

sentences.zh: 又使河東，論韓絳築囉兀二砦：「始調外郡稍遠邊城前後三十萬夫，遼州最為窮僻，然猶上戶配夫四百三十四，僦直計三千緡，下者十六人，其直十萬。

translations.literal: Again sent to Hedong, discussing Han Jiang's building of Luowu and two stockades: "At first mobilizing from outer prefectures slightly distant from frontier cities, front and back three hundred thousand laborers; Liaozhou was most poor and remote, yet still upper households were assigned four hundred thirty-four laborers, hired wages totaling three thousand strings; lower ones sixteen men, wages one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Sent again to Hedong, he criticized Han Jiang's construction of Luowu and two other stockades: "The project initially conscripted three hundred thousand laborers from outer prefectures far from the frontier. Liaozhou was the poorest and most remote, yet even wealthy households were assessed four hundred thirty-four laborers at a hire cost of three thousand strings, while poorer ones owed sixteen men at a cost of one hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 輦運所經二十二驛，宣撫司不先告期，轉運使臨時督辦，致民皆破產，上下莫敢言。

translations.literal: Transport carts passed through twenty-two post stations; the Pacification Commission did not announce dates in advance; the transport commissioner supervised matters on the spot; causing the people all to bankrupt their estates; above and below none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies passed through twenty-two post stations. The Pacification Commission gave no advance notice, and the transport commissioner rushed orders at the last minute. The people were ruined, and no one from top to bottom dared complain.

sentences.zh: 獨遼守李宏能約民力所勝，而饋不失期，顧以訴其實，翻令鞫罪。

translations.literal: Only Liaozhou Prefect Li Hong was able to limit conscription to what the people's strength could bear, yet supplies did not miss their deadlines; yet for reporting the facts he was instead ordered interrogated for crime.
translations.idiomatic: Only Liaozhou Prefect Li Hong managed to keep levies within what the people could bear while meeting supply deadlines. Yet when he reported the truth, he was himself put on trial.

sentences.zh: 願貸被劾官吏，其芻糧在道者隨所至受之，使已困之民咸蒙德澤。」

translations.literal: I wish to pardon the impeached officials; the fodder and grain on the road wherever they arrive let it be received; so that the already distressed people all receive imperial grace."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the prosecuted officials be pardoned and that fodder and grain in transit be accepted wherever it arrives, so that an already exhausted populace may feel the emperor's mercy."

sentences.zh: 神宗皆從之。

translations.literal: Shenzong adopted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong approved all of these requests.

sentences.zh: 坐劾李定親喪匿服，罷御史，檢正中書戶房，固辭，乃知韓城縣。

translations.literal: For impeaching Li Ding for concealing mourning during a parent's death, he was dismissed as censor, appointed Rectifier in the Household Section of the Secretariat, firmly declined, and was then made magistrate of Hancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: After impeaching Li Ding for failing to observe mourning for a parent, he was removed as censor and offered the post of Rectifier in the Secretariat's Household Section. He declined firmly and was appointed magistrate of Hancheng County.

sentences.zh: 詔往鄜延議畫地界，育言：「保疆不如持約，持約不如敦信。

translations.literal: An edict sent him to Fuyan to discuss demarcating borders; Yu said: "Preserving territory is not as good as maintaining treaties; maintaining treaties is not as good as honoring good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to Fuyan to negotiate border demarcation, Yu argued, "Defending territory is less reliable than honoring treaties, and honoring treaties is less reliable than keeping faith.

sentences.zh: 前日疆埸嘗嚴矣，一旦約敗兵，鬥者跌於前，耕者侵於後，是封溝不足恃也。

translations.literal: Formerly the frontier was once strict; once a treaty failed, troops fought; fighters fell in front, plowmen encroached in the rear—fortified ditches are not to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier was once heavily guarded, yet when a treaty collapsed soldiers fought in front while farmers encroached from behind. Fortified ditches alone cannot be trusted.

sentences.zh: 使人左去而兵革右興，金繒朝委而烽煙夕舉，是持約不足恃也。

translations.literal: Envoys depart left while arms rise right; gold and silk delivered in the morning while beacon fires raised at evening—maintaining treaties is not to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys depart in the morning while arms are raised by evening; silk tribute is delivered at dawn while beacon fires blaze at dusk. Treaties alone cannot be trusted either.

sentences.zh: 今我見利而加兵，當講好之後，復自立界，不亦愧乎！」

translations.literal: Now we see profit and add troops; after making peace, again establish boundaries on our own—is this not shameful!"
translations.idiomatic: We now seize an advantage and march troops in. After making peace we redraw the border on our own. Is that not shameful?"

sentences.zh: 安南行營郭逵、趙卨以兵十萬伐交阯，行及長沙，病死相屬，逵、卨又不輯睦，育疏其不便，不從。

translations.literal: The Annan expeditionary camp's Guo Kui and Zhao Jie with one hundred thousand troops attacked Jiaozhi; marching to Changsha, deaths from illness followed one after another; Kui and Jie also did not harmonize; Yu memorialized its disadvantages; not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Kui and Zhao Jie of the Annan expedition led one hundred thousand troops against Jiaozhi. By the time they reached Changsha, deaths from disease were mounting, and the two commanders quarreled. Yu memorialized against the campaign, but his advice was ignored.

sentences.zh: 久之，知河中府，加直集賢院，徙鳳翔，以直龍圖閣鎮秦州。

translations.literal: After a long time, governor of Hezhong prefecture, added as Hanlin Compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, transferred to Fengxiang, as Compiler at the Hall of Dragon Designs garrisoning Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was governor of Hezhong, appointed Hanlin Compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, transferred to Fengxiang, and garrisoned Qinzhou as Compiler at the Hall of Dragon Designs.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，召為太常少卿，改光祿卿、樞密都承旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, summoned as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, changed to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Chief Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanyou era he was recalled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Chief Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 劉安世暴其閨門不肅，出知熙州。

translations.literal: Liu Anshi exposed his disorder in the inner quarters; sent out as prefect of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Anshi exposed scandal in his private life, and he was sent out as prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 時又議棄質孤、勝如兩堡，育爭之曰：「熙河以蘭州為要塞，此兩堡者蘭州之蔽也。

translations.literal: At the time there was again debate over abandoning Zhigu and Sheng Ru two forts; Yu contended: "Xihe takes Lanzhou as its strategic pass; these two forts are Lanzhou's cover.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated abandoning the forts at Zhigu and Sheng Ru, Yu objected, "The Xihe region hinges on Lanzhou as its stronghold. These two forts shield Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 棄之則蘭州危，蘭州危則熙河有腰膂之憂矣。」

translations.literal: Abandon them and Lanzhou is endangered; Lanzhou endangered and Xihe has worry for its waist and backbone."
translations.idiomatic: Abandon them and Lanzhou falls into peril; if Lanzhou is imperiled, the whole Xihe region loses its backbone."

sentences.zh: 又請城李諾平、汝遮川，曰：「此趙充國屯田古榆塞之地也。」

translations.literal: Again he requested fortifying Linuoping and Ruzhechuan, saying: "This is the land of Zhao Chongguo's military colony at ancient Yu Pass."
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to fortify Linuoping and Ruzhechuan, saying, "This is where Zhao Chongguo once established military colonies at the ancient Yu Pass."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply.
translations.idiomatic: His petition received no reply.

sentences.zh: 入為給事中、戶部侍郎，卒。

translations.literal: Entered service as Supervising Censor and Vice Minister of the Household Bureau; died.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Supervising Censor and Vice Minister of the Household Bureau, and died there.

sentences.zh: 高宗紹興中，采其抗論棄地及進築之策，贈寶文閣學士。

translations.literal: In Gaozong's Shaoxing era, adopting his arguments against abandoning territory and his proposals for advancing construction, posthumously granted Academician of the Hall of Treasured Culture.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Gaozong's Shaoxing era, the court honored his opposition to territorial abandonment and his proposals for frontier fortification by posthumously granting him the title Academician of the Hall of Treasured Culture.

sentences.zh: 田京，字簡之，世居滄州，其後徙亳州鹿邑。

translations.literal: Tian Jing, style Jianzhi, for generations dwelt in Cangzhou; afterward moved to Luyi in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jing, styled Jianzhi, came from a family long settled in Cangzhou that later moved to Luyi in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，調蜀州司法參軍，自秦州觀察推官改秘書省著作佐郎，為大理寺詳斷官。

translations.literal: Passed the jinshi examination, appointed legal assistant of Shuzhou, from investigative magistrate of Qinzhou changed to Assistant Editor in the Secretariat, made detailed adjudication officer of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi graduate, he served as legal assistant in Shuzhou, rose from investigative magistrate in Qinzhou to Assistant Editor in the Secretariat, and became a detailed adjudication officer of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 趙元昊反，侍讀學士李仲容薦京知兵法，召試中書，擢通判鎮戎軍。

translations.literal: When Zhao Yuan Hao rebelled, Attendant Reader Li Zhongrong recommended Jing as knowing military methods; summoned for examination at the Secretariat, promoted as military supervisor of Zhenrong Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yuan Hao rebelled, Attendant Reader Li Zhongrong recommended Tian Jing for his knowledge of military affairs. Summoned for examination at the Secretariat, he was promoted to military supervisor of Zhenrong Army.

sentences.zh: 夏守贇為陝西經略使，奏兼管勾隨軍糧料。

translations.literal: Xia Shouyun as Shaanxi frontier commissioner memorialized that he concurrently manage expedition army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Shouyun served as Shaanxi frontier commissioner, he had Tian Jing appointed to manage expedition army provisions.

sentences.zh: 入對，陳方略，賜五品服。

translations.literal: Entered for audience, expounded strategy, granted fifth-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court, presented strategic plans, and was granted fifth-rank robes.

sentences.zh: 尋為經略安撫判官。

translations.literal: Soon made judicial intendant of the frontier pacification commission.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became judicial intendant on the frontier pacification staff.

sentences.zh: 守贇既罷，以武略應運籌決勝科，及試秘閣，與他科偕試六論，京自以記誦非所長，引去。

translations.literal: After Shouyun was dismissed, through the Military Strategy Responsive Strategy and Decisive Victory examination category, when reaching the Hall of Secrets examination, together with other categories jointly tested on six essays, Jing considered memorization not his strength and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After Xia Shouyun was dismissed, Tian Jing entered the Military Strategy examination track. When the Hall of Secrets examination required six essays alongside other categories, he withdrew, judging memorization not his strength.

sentences.zh: 又參夏竦軍事。

translations.literal: Again joined Xia Song's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Xia Song's military staff.

sentences.zh: 會遺翰林學士晁宗愨即軍中問攻守孰便，眾欲大舉入討，京曰：「夏人之不道久矣，未易破也。

translations.literal: When the late Hanlin Academician Chao Zongque came to the army to ask whether attack or defense was preferable, the multitude wished to launch a great expedition to punish them; Jing said: "The Tangut's wickedness has long continued; they are not easily broken.
translations.idiomatic: When the late Hanlin Academician Chao Zongque came to camp to ask whether attack or defense was wiser, most favored a major punitive expedition. Tian Jing said, "The Tangut have long been unruly. They will not be easily defeated.

sentences.zh: 今欲驅不習之師，深入敵境，與之角勝負，此兵家所忌，師出必敗。」

translations.literal: Now wishing to drive troops unaccustomed to battle, deep into enemy territory, to contest victory with them—this is what military strategists forbid; the army goes out and must be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: To drive inexperienced troops deep into enemy territory and contest them on their own ground is exactly what military strategists warn against. Such an expedition is doomed to fail."

sentences.zh: 或曰：「不如講和。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Better to make peace."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Perhaps we should negotiate peace instead."

sentences.zh: 京曰：「敵兵未嘗挫，安肯降我哉？」

translations.literal: Jing said: "The enemy's troops have never been broken—how would they willingly submit to us?"
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jing replied, "Their army has never been broken. Why would they willingly submit to us?"

sentences.zh: 未幾，元昊使黃延德叩延州乞降，以奇兵出原、渭，敗大將任福。

translations.literal: Before long, Yuan Hao sent Huang Yande to knock at Yanzhou begging surrender, while with surprise troops he marched out from Yuan and Wei and defeated the great general Ren Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuan Hao sent Huang Yande to Yanzhou offering surrender while dispatching surprise forces from Yuan and Wei to defeat the great general Ren Fu.

sentences.zh: 夏竦素不悅京，坐是改通判廬州，徙知邵武軍，提點河北路刑獄事。
