translations.literal: Xia Song had long not favored Jing; because of this changed to military supervisor of Luzhou, transferred to know Shaowu Army, judicial intendant of Hebei Circuit punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song had long disliked Tian Jing. For this he was demoted to military supervisor of Luzhou, then transferred to command Shaowu Army and serve as Hebei judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 乃上言：「請擇要官守滄、衛，鑿西山石臼廢道以限戎馬，義勇聚教，復給糧，置卒守烽燧，用奇正法訓兵，徙戰馬內地以息邊費。」

translations.literal: Then he submitted: "I request selecting key officials to guard Cang and Wei, cutting through the stone mortar abandoned road in the western mountains to limit barbarian horses, gathering and training volunteers, restoring grain allotments, posting soldiers to guard beacon towers, using irregular and regular methods to train troops, moving war horses to the interior to rest frontier expenses."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, saying, "Please select key officials to guard Cangzhou and Weizhou, reopen the abandoned stone-mortar road in the western hills to block barbarian cavalry, muster and train local volunteers with rations restored, post troops to watch the beacon towers, drill troops in both orthodox and unorthodox tactics, and move war horses inland to reduce frontier costs."

sentences.zh: 凡十餘事，仁宗頗嘉納之。

translations.literal: More than ten items in all; Renzong fairly praised and adopted them.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial listed more than a dozen proposals, which Emperor Renzong largely praised and adopted.

sentences.zh: 入為開封府判官，坐械囚送獄道死，出知蔡州，徙相、邢二州，復提點河北刑獄事。

translations.literal: Entered service as judicial intendant of Kaifeng Prefecture; punished because shackled prisoners died on the road while being sent to prison; sent out as prefect of Caizhou, transferred to Xiang and Xing prefectures, again judicial intendant of Hebei punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as judicial intendant of Kaifeng Prefecture but was demoted after shackled prisoners died en route to jail. He was sent out as prefect of Caizhou, then transferred to Xiang and Xing, and again served as Hebei judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 王則據恩州反，京縋城趣南關，入驍健營撫士卒。

translations.literal: Wang Ze seized Enzhou and rebelled; Jing descended the city wall by rope hastening to the South Gate, entered the Elite Brave Camp to reassure soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ze seized Enzhou and rebelled, Tian Jing lowered himself from the city wall by rope and raced to the South Gate, entering the Elite Brave Camp to rally the troops.

sentences.zh: 保州振武兵焚民居欲應賊，京捕斬之乃定。

translations.literal: Baozhou Zhenwu troops burned civilians' dwellings wishing to join the rebels; Jing captured and executed them, and only then was it settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenwu troops in Baozhou burned civilian homes in sympathy with the rebels. Tian Jing captured and executed them, and order was restored.

sentences.zh: 賊遣其黨崔象偽出降，京以其持妖言惑眾，又斬以徇，由是營兵二十六指揮在外者皆懾服，不敢叛。

translations.literal: The rebels sent their partisan Cui Xiang to feign surrender; Jing because he held sorcerous words to delude the masses again executed him to display, and thereby the twenty-six commands of garrison troops outside all were awed into submission and did not dare rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent one Cui Xiang to feign surrender; Jing judged that he spread sorcerous talk to mislead the people and had him executed as a warning. Thereafter the twenty-six garrison commands stationed outside the city were cowed into obedience and dared not mutiny.

sentences.zh: 州之南關，民眾多如城中，得不陷賊，京有功焉。

translations.literal: At the prefecture's south gate the populace were as numerous as within the city; they were able not to fall to the rebels—Jing had merit in this.
translations.idiomatic: The south suburb of the prefecture held a population as large as the city itself and did not fall to the rebels; Jing deserved credit for that.

sentences.zh: 京督士攻城甚力，賊繫京妻子乘城迫使呼曰：「毋亟攻，城中將屠我輩矣。」

translations.literal: Jing supervised the troops in assaulting the city with great force; the rebels bound Jing's wife and children, mounted the wall, and forced them to call out: "Do not press the attack hastily—the city will slaughter us all."
translations.idiomatic: Jing drove the assault with great vigor. The rebels bound his wife and children, brought them onto the wall, and forced them to shout, "Do not press the attack—the city will slaughter us!"

sentences.zh: 京叱諸軍益進攻，注矢仰射，殺其家四人。

translations.literal: Jing shouted at the armies to press the attack harder, aimed arrows upward and shot, and killed four of his family.
translations.idiomatic: Jing ordered the troops to press the attack harder, drew his bow, shot upward, and killed four members of his own family.

sentences.zh: 賊知京無所顧，乃牽妻子去，恩州平。

translations.literal: The rebels knew Jing had nothing left to care for and therefore dragged his wife and children away; Enzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Jing would spare nothing, the rebels dragged his family away, and Enzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 以不能預察賊，降監鄆州稅。

translations.literal: Because he could not foresee the rebels in advance, he was demoted to supervise Yanzhou tax collection.
translations.idiomatic: For failing to detect the rebellion in advance, he was demoted to supervisor of tax collection at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，駐泊都監田斌亦以賊發不能捕，待罪兵間，及城破，從諸將入，以功遷宮苑副使，而京獨被謫。

translations.literal: Earlier, garrison commander Tian Bin had also because the rebels rose been unable to capture them and awaited punishment among the troops; when the city fell he followed the generals in and for merit was promoted to vice commissioner of the Palace Parks, while Jing alone was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, garrison commander Tian Bin had likewise failed to capture the rebels when they rose and awaited punishment in the ranks; when the city fell he entered with the other generals and was promoted to vice commissioner of the Palace Parks for his service, while Jing alone was punished.

sentences.zh: 御史言失察賊過輕，忘家為國義獨重，不宜左遷，乃徙通判兗州。

translations.literal: The censor said the offense of failing to detect the rebels was too light a penalty, that forgetting family for the state's righteousness was uniquely weighty, and that he should not be transferred downward; he was therefore moved to vice-prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A censor argued that the penalty for failing to foresee the rebellion was too harsh, that Jing's sacrifice of family for the state outweighed the fault, and that he should not be demoted; he was instead made vice-prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 又徙知江陰軍，知密州，歷提點淮南刑獄事、京西轉運使，累遷兵部員外郎、直史館、知滄州轉運使。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to be military prefect of Jiangyin, prefect of Mizhou, successively judicial intendant of Huainan criminal affairs and Jingxi transport commissioner, and through successive promotions became Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of War, Direct Historiography, and Cangzhou transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made military prefect of Jiangyin and prefect of Mizhou, served as judicial intendant for Huainan and as Jingxi transport commissioner, and rose through successive posts to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of War, appointment to the Direct Historiography, and transport commissioner of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 京能招輯流民，為之給田除稅租，凡增戶萬七千，特遷工部郎中。

translations.literal: Jing was able to gather and settle displaced persons, provide them fields and remit rent and tax, and in all increased households by seventeen thousand; he was specially promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was skilled at gathering and resettling refugees, granting them land and remitting rent and taxes; he registered seventeen thousand new households and was specially promoted to director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 然傳者謂流民之數多不實，又強為人田非其所樂，侵民稅地，仿古屯田法，其後法不成，所給種錢牛價，民多不償，鞭笞督責，至累年不能平，公私皆患之。

translations.literal: Yet transmitters say the number of displaced persons was largely untrue, and that he also forced people onto fields they did not desire, encroached on taxpayers' land, and imitated ancient tuntian methods; afterward the method did not succeed, the seed money and ox prices given were mostly not repaid, and with flogging he pressed collection until for years it could not be settled—both public and private were troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rumor held that the refugee numbers were greatly inflated, that he forced men onto land they did not want, encroached on taxpayers' fields, and imitated the ancient frontier-colony system. The scheme ultimately failed: seed loans and ox prices went largely unpaid, and years of flogging to compel repayment left both government and people burdened.

sentences.zh: 擢天章閣待制、陝西都轉運使，改兵部郎中，復知滄州，拜右諫議大夫，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin associate at the Tianzhang Pavilion and Shaanxi chief transport commissioner, changed to Director in the Ministry of War, again made prefect of Cangzhou, appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin associate at the Tianzhang Pavilion and chief transport commissioner for Shaanxi, reappointed director in the Ministry of War and prefect of Cangzhou, made Right Remonstrance Grandee, and died.

sentences.zh: 京喜論議，然語繁而迂，頗通兵戰、曆算、雜家之術。

translations.literal: Jing delighted in discourse and debate, yet his language was prolix and circuitous; he was quite versed in military campaigning, calendrical calculation, and miscellaneous schools' arts.
translations.idiomatic: Jing loved debate, though his speech was wordy and abstruse; he was well versed in military science, calendrical calculation, and various technical arts.

sentences.zh: 為人尚氣節，少時與常山董士廉、汾陰郭京相友善，俱以倜儻聞。

translations.literal: As a man he valued integrity and spirit; in youth he was friendly with Changshan Dong Shilian and Fenyin Guo Jing, and all were known for bold unconventionality.
translations.idiomatic: He prized integrity and spirit; in his youth he befriended Dong Shilian of Changshan and Guo Jing of Fenyin, and all three were known for their bold, unconventional character.

sentences.zh: 著《天人流術》、《通儒子》十數書，又有奏議十卷。

translations.literal: He authored more than ten books including Heavenly Human Flow Arts and Comprehensive Confucian Master, and also had ten juan of memorials and proposals.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote more than ten works, including Heavenly Human Flow Arts and Comprehensive Confucian Master, as well as ten juan of memorials and policy proposals.

sentences.zh: 論曰：人臣之職，當奮不顧身，而庸人怯夫於國事則噎喑而不言，若胡越肥瘠之不相干，如張述者其亦忠且果矣。

translations.literal: The commentary says: The duty of a minister is to strive without regard for his person, yet mediocre men and cowards on state affairs choke silent and do not speak, as if Hu and Yue's fatness and leanness were unrelated to one another—as Zhang Shu was, he too was loyal and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: A minister's duty is to give himself wholly to the state, yet mediocre and timid men fall mute on public affairs, as though the welfare of far Hu and near Yue were none of their concern. Zhang Shu, at least, was loyal and resolute.

sentences.zh: 黃震指李溥忤權臣，胡順之擊強宗，為眾人所不敢為；

translations.literal: Huang Zhen denounced Li Pu in defiance of powerful ministers; Hu Shunzhi struck powerful clans—doing what the multitude did not dare do;
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhen denounced Li Pu in defiance of powerful ministers; Hu Shunzhi struck down powerful clans—deeds others dared not attempt;

sentences.zh: 陳貫論兵事，范祥畫邊計，皆一時雋士。

translations.literal: Chen Guan discoursed on military affairs; Fan Xiang drafted frontier plans—all were outstanding men of their time.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guan discoursed on military affairs and Fan Xiang drafted frontier strategy; each was an outstanding talent of his day.

sentences.zh: 妖盜竊發，京出孤力保城南，置妻孥之憂，先登示賊，其勇蓋可壯也。

translations.literal: When sorcerous bandits rose in secret, Jing went out alone to defend the south of the city, set aside worry for wife and children, took the lead in ascending to show the rebels—his courage may indeed be called inspiring.
translations.idiomatic: When the sorcerer-rebel rose, Jing alone held the south suburb, set aside concern for wife and children, and led the assault to show the enemy his resolve—courage worthy of admiration indeed.
